definition_en: a person who makes art, or a skilled performer
core_image: 画室里一个人正给老人画肖像
scene: 画室里，一个人支起画架，正给一位老人画肖像。 The artist painted a portrait of the old man.
sceneCN: 这里 artist 是「画家」（第 1 个义项：从事绘画创作的人）；句意为这位画家画了一幅老人的肖像。

senses.title: A maker of art
senses.definition: a person who paints, draws or makes works of art
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、素描或创作艺术品的人
senses.example: The artist painted a portrait of the old man.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家画了一幅老人的肖像。
senses.why: Art is the skill and the person suffix marks the doer, so the maker of pictures is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: art 是技艺，表人的后缀标记执行者，所以作画的人就是第一义。

senses.title: A skilled performer
senses.definition: a person who performs an art with great skill
senses.definitionCN: 以高超技艺表演某种艺术的人
senses.example: The young artist sang beautifully on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻艺人在台上唱得很动听。
senses.why: The same skill can be shown on a stage, so a singer or dancer also carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 同样的技艺也能在舞台上展现，所以歌手或舞者也用这个名称。

intro.en: The recorded history of artist is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 artist 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Ars meant skill, craft or art.
items.cn: ars 意为技艺、手艺或艺术。

items.en: French artiste named a person skilled in an art.
items.cn: 法语 artiste 指擅长某种艺术的人。

items.en: English borrowed artist for a maker of art.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 artist，指艺术创作者。

items.en: Later it also named skilled singers and dancers.
items.cn: 后来它也指技艺娴熟的歌手与舞者。

items.en: Today it covers painters, musicians and street performers.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖画家、音乐家与街头艺人。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one maker of art.
entries.definitionCN: 指多位艺术创作者。

entries.definition: The skill that the artist works with.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家所运用的技艺。

entries.definition: The adjective for art and its makers.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指艺术与创作者的。

entries.definition: It names the maker of pictures only.
entries.definitionCN: 只指作画的人。

entries.definition: A general word for someone who makes things.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指创造事物的人。

entries.definition: It names someone who acts or sings before people.
entries.definitionCN: 指在众人面前表演或演唱的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: art means creative skill and -ist means the person: an artist is the one who works the skill.
normal.cn: art 表示创造性的技艺，-ist 表示人：artist 就是运用这门技艺的人。

normal.en: The same family also gives art and artistic.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 art 与 artistic。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase a young artist.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「一位年轻艺术家」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of artist in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 artist 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: a person who makes art, or a skilled performer.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「艺术家」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a person painting a portrait of an old man in a studio.
abstract.cn: 想象画室里一个人正给老人画肖像。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of artist grows from one core image: a person painting a portrait of an old man in a studio.
sensesIntro.cn: artist 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：画室里一个人正给老人画肖像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person painting a portrait of an old man in a studio
core.cn: 核心意象：画室里一个人正给老人画肖像

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: A maker of art.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：画家、艺术家。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: A skilled performer.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：能手、艺人。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: A maker of art / A skilled performer.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：画家、艺术家、能手、艺人。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a further use: A skilled performer.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：能手、艺人。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖意义的边缘：画家、艺术家、能手、艺人。

It names the doer of an action.

definition_en: to look at something again in order to judge or learn
core_image: 台灯下摊开的笔记，旁边放着一支红笔
scene: 考试前夜，她坐在台灯下复习整学期的笔记。 Before the exam, she sat under a lamp and reviewed the notes from the whole term.
sceneCN: 这里 review 是「复习」（第 2 个义项：为学习而重看）；句意：考试前夜，她坐在台灯下复习整学期的笔记。

derivatives.zh: 评论者；审查者
可审查的

senses.title: Looking again
senses.definition: to examine something again
senses.definitionCN: 再次检查某事物
senses.example: The committee will review the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会将审查这项计划。
senses.why: Re- means again, so review is to look again.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为再一次，所以 review 就是再看一遍。

senses.title: Studying again
senses.definition: to study material again before a test
senses.definitionCN: 考试前再次学习材料
senses.example: She reviewed her notes before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她复习了笔记。
senses.why: Looking again turns into study when a test is near.
senses.whyCN: 临近考试时，重看就变成了复习。

senses.title: Judging a work
senses.definition: to write an opinion about a book, film or play
senses.definitionCN: 对书、电影或戏剧写出看法
senses.example: He reviews films for a local paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他为当地报纸写影评。
senses.why: A review looks again and then judges.
senses.whyCN: 评论是先重看再评判。

intro.en: Review comes from French reveue, a viewing again, from revoir, to see again.
intro.cn: review 源自法语 reveue（再看一次），来自 revoir（再看）。

items.en: Reveue means a viewing again.
items.cn: reveue 意为再看一次。

items.en: Revoir joins re- to voir, to see.
items.cn: revoir 由 re- 与 voir（看）组成。

items.en: Videre, to see, is the deeper root.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看）是更深的词根。

items.en: Review enters English as a look back at something.
items.cn: review 以「回看某物」之意进入英语。

items.en: It also means judging a book or film.
items.cn: 它也指评判一本书或一部电影。

note.en: Review looks again, while revise changes what is seen.
note.cn: review 是再看一遍，revise 是修改所看的内容。

entries.definition: to look at something carefully

normalIntro.en: Review is a second look with a purpose.
normalIntro.cn: review 是有目的的第二次观看。

normal.en: A book review gives an opinion about a book.
normal.cn: book review 是对一本书给出看法。

normal.en: Under review means being examined.
normal.cn: under review 意为正在被审查。

normal.en: Review notes means study them again.
normal.cn: review notes 意为再学一遍笔记。

abstract.en: Picture a red pen moving over old notes.
abstract.cn: 想象红笔在旧笔记上移动。

abstract.en: Imagine a film critic watching a movie twice.
abstract.cn: 想象影评人把一部电影看两遍。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror that lets you see yesterday again.
abstract.cn: 想象一面能让你再看一遍昨天的镜子。

examples.cn: 老师和我们一起回顾了这堂课。

examples.en: Her review of the novel was very kind.
examples.cn: 她对这部小说的评论非常友善。

examples.en: The case is still under review.
examples.cn: 这个案件仍在审查中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ view（看）」——再看一遍，就是回顾、复习、评论。

sensesIntro.en: Review means to look again, whether at a plan, at notes, or at a work of art.
sensesIntro.cn: review 指再看一遍，无论对象是计划、笔记还是艺术作品。

core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下的旧笔记与红笔。

branches.en: Looking again is the core act.
branches.cn: 再看一遍是核心行为。

branches.cn: 复习是在考试前重复这一看。

branches.en: Judging follows the second look.

branches.en: Both checking and studying begin with looking again.

branches.en: A review looks back and then gives an opinion.
branches.cn: 评论先回看，再给出看法。

intro.en: Review combines re-, again, with the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: review 由 re-（再）与拉丁词根 vid（看）组成。

latinIntro.en: The path runs from Latin videre to French voir and then English review.
latinIntro.cn: 这条路径从拉丁语 videre 到法语 voir，再到英语 review。

items.exampleCN: vid 出现在 video 与 evident 中。

latinEntries.exampleCN: videre 是许多与视觉有关单词的基础。

definition_en: the quality or state of being hot, or the energy that produces warmth; also to make something warm
core_image: 炉火把锅底烧红，锅里的油开始冒起细小的气泡，热气向上升腾
scene: 厨房里，厨师把平底锅放到灶火上，说 Heat the oil before you add the onions.
sceneCN: 这里 heat 是动词「加热」（第 8 个义项：把食物或液体加热到可以烹饪的温度）；句意为先把油烧热，再下洋葱。图中可辨识物件：平底锅、灶火、油、洋葱。

senses.title: Thermal energy in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学意义上的热、热能
senses.definition: the energy that transfers from a warmer body to a cooler one, measured in joules
senses.definitionCN: 从较热物体传向较冷物体的能量，以焦耳计量
senses.example: The experiment measured how much heat the metal bar absorbed.
senses.exampleCN: 实验测量了金属棒吸收了多少热量。
senses.why: The physical sense is the modern, countable-in-laboratory version of the old quality 'being hot'.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是旧义「热的性质」在实验室里可计量的现代版本。

senses.title: Hot weather
senses.definition: a period of unusually high air temperature, especially in summer
senses.definitionCN: 气温异常偏高的一段时间，尤指夏季
senses.example: The heat kept the whole town indoors until evening.
senses.exampleCN: 高温让全镇的人一直躲在家里直到傍晚。
senses.why: Weather talk applied the mass noun to the air itself, so 'the heat' became a way to name a hot spell.
senses.whyCN: 谈天气时把这个不可数名词用到了空气上，「the heat」便成了指一段暑热的说法。

senses.title: A source of warmth
senses.titleCN: 供暖；炉火或暖气带来的温暖
senses.definition: warmth supplied by a fire, radiator or heating system
senses.definitionCN: 由炉火、暖气片或供暖系统提供的温暖
senses.example: They sat close to the stove because the heat reached only the front room.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐得离炉子很近，因为热气只到得了前屋。
senses.why: A fire is both the hot thing and the warmth it gives off, so the same noun names the source and the effect.
senses.whyCN: 火既是热的东西，也是它散发的温暖，因此同一个名词兼指来源与效果。

senses.title: Body temperature and fever
senses.definition: the warmth of a living body, especially when it is higher than normal
senses.definitionCN: 活体的温度，尤指高于正常水平时
senses.example: The nurse checked the child for heat around the forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 护士摸了摸孩子的额头，看有没有发热。
senses.why: Living bodies produce warmth, so the noun moved from the fire to the body and then to illness.
senses.whyCN: 活体自己产生热量，名词便从炉火移到身体，再移到疾病上。

senses.title: Pungency in food
senses.definition: the sharp burning sensation given by chilli, pepper or mustard
senses.definitionCN: 辣椒、胡椒或芥末带来的尖锐灼烧感
senses.example: The heat of the sauce surprised everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁的辣度让桌上所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The sensation is literally a burning warmth on the tongue, so the temperature word was borrowed for taste.
senses.whyCN: 那种感觉本就是舌头上的灼热，于是温度词被借去形容味道。

senses.title: Intensity of feeling or pressure
senses.titleCN: 情绪或局势的激烈程度
senses.definition: the most intense part of an activity, argument or period of pressure
senses.definitionCN: 活动、争论或压力最激烈的阶段
senses.example: In the heat of the debate, nobody noticed the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论最激烈的时候，没人去看钟。
senses.why: Strong feeling was pictured as a fire burning at its hottest, so 'in the heat of' marks the peak.
senses.whyCN: 强烈情绪被想象成烧得最旺的火，因此「in the heat of」标出最炽烈的顶点。

senses.title: A preliminary race
senses.definition: one of several earlier races whose winners go on to the final
senses.definitionCN: 决赛之前举行的若干场比赛，胜者进入决赛
senses.example: She won her heat and advanced to the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢下了自己的预赛，进入决赛。
senses.why: Each preliminary race was felt to 'heat up' the competitors; the sporting sense is a separate branch of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 每场预赛都被看作让选手「热起来」的环节；这一体育义是同一名词的另一条分支。

senses.title: To make something warm
senses.definition: to raise the temperature of something so that it becomes warm or ready to use
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的温度，使其变热或可以使用
senses.example: He heated the soup until it steamed.
senses.exampleCN: 他把汤加热到冒热气。
senses.why: The verb is the plain causative of the noun: to heat something is to put heat into it.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词的普通使役形式：给某物加热，就是把热放进某物里。

intro.en: Heat is a native English word, not a borrowing. Old English had hǣtu 'heat' beside hāt 'hot', and the noun has kept the same shape in meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: heat 是英语本族词，不是借词。古英语在 hāt「热的」之外还有 hǣtu「热」，这个名词的含义千年来基本未变。

items.en: Hǣtu meant 'heat, warmth, the quality of being hot' and was formed from hāt 'hot'.
items.cn: hǣtu 意为「热、温暖、热的性质」，由 hāt「热的」构成。

items.en: The same stock appears in Old High German heizī and modern German Hitze, so the word is shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 同一词源出现在古高地德语 heizī 与现代德语 Hitze，说明这个词在日耳曼语族内共用。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is the root *kai- 'heat', but this is a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 通常把词根构拟为 *kai-「热」，但这是重构形式，不是有记录的实际词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century heat became a technical term for transferred thermal energy, and the older everyday senses remained beside it.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，heat 成为指传递热能的术语，而更早的日常义仍与它并存。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the pre-Germanic origin rests on a reconstruction, and the first date of the sporting sense is recorded only loosely.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：日耳曼语之前的来源建立在重构之上；体育义的最早年代也只有粗略记载。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to heat but come from other roots; group two holds words for warmth or temperature that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近但词根不同的词；第二组是表示温暖或温度、范围有别的词。

entries.definition: The grain, from Old English hwǣte; it contains the letters of heat but has no connection to warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 指小麦，来自古英语 hwǣte；字母与 heat 相近，但与「热」毫无关系。

entries.definition: To strike something, from Old English hittan; the vowel and the meaning both keep it apart from heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指击打，来自古英语 hittan；元音与词义都使它不同于 heat。

entries.definition: To pay attention to something, from Old English hēdan 'to guard, observe'; it is not related to heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指留意、注意，来自古英语 hēdan「看守、观察」；与 heat 不同源。

entries.definition: An old word for a non-Christian pagan, from Old English hǣthen; the shared letters hide a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指非基督教的异教徒，来自古英语 hǣthen；相同的字母掩盖了不同的来源。

entries.definition: A moderate, comfortable degree of heat; heat itself can be far more intense or technical.
entries.definitionCN: 温和舒适的热度；heat 本身可以强烈得多，也可以作为技术术语。

entries.definition: The measured degree of hotness of a body or place, rather than the energy or the sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或场所被测出的冷热程度，而非能量本身或主观感受。

entries.definition: A body temperature above normal caused by illness; heat is the wider word for any warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常体温升高；heat 是泛指一切热度的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: The flame itself that produces heat; heat names the warmth or energy that the fire gives off.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生热的火焰本身；heat 指火焰释放出的温暖或能量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native root, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的英语本族词根、真实复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hǣtu 'heat' stands beside hāt 'hot', so the noun and the adjective have always travelled together.
normal.cn: 古英语 hǣtu「热」与 hāt「热的」并立，名词与形容词一直同行。

normal.en: Compounds mark the senses: heat wave, body heat, heat source, heat loss, heat transfer.
normal.cn: 复合词标出各义项：热浪、体温、热源、热量损失、热传递。

normal.en: The verb family runs heat, heats, heated, heating, heater.
normal.cn: 动词词族包括 heat、heats、heated、heating、heater。

normal.en: The phrase 'in the heat of' always points to the most intense moment of an activity.
normal.cn: 「in the heat of」这一短语总是指活动最激烈的那一刻。

normal.en: Sporting heats are early races that heat up the competition before the final.
normal.cn: 体育中的 heat 是决赛前让竞争「热起来」的预赛。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle that keeps singing until the whole kitchen feels warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只一直鸣响的水壶，直到整个厨房都暖起来。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that gets hotter the longer it lasts, until words are all sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象一场越吵越热的争论，最后每句话都成了火星。

abstract.en: Picture a single coal carried from a fire into a cold room, still glowing in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从火里带到冷屋的炭，仍在手心发着光。

examples.en: The heat from the radiator dried the wet coats overnight.
examples.cn: 暖气片的热量一夜之间把湿外套烘干了。

examples.en: Add the spices only after the oil begins to heat.
examples.cn: 等油开始变热后再下香料。

examples.en: The runners were assigned to different heats by their qualifying times.
examples.cn: 选手按资格赛成绩被分到不同的预赛组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热特」——把东西放到火上热一热，热就出来了

root: 古英语 hǣtu「热」，由 hāt「热的」构成，属日耳曼语族，与古高地德语 heizī、现代德语 Hitze 同源；更深词根通常重构为 *kai-「热」，属重构形式，非实际记录词。无拉丁语同族来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: warmth is first a physical quantity, then the weather, a fire, a body, a burning taste, a peak of feeling, a preliminary race, and finally the act of making something warm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：热先是物理量，然后是天气、炉火、身体、灼烧的味觉、情绪的顶点、预赛，最后是给东西加热的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red stove bottom with oil beginning to bubble above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧红的锅底，上面的油开始冒泡。

branches.en: MEASURED ENERGY: physics turns the old quality into joules that can be counted.
branches.cn: 可计量的能量：物理学把旧时的性质变成可数的焦耳。

branches.en: WEATHER AND FIRE: the same noun names a hot spell and the warmth a stove gives out.
branches.cn: 天气与炉火：同一个名词既指一段暑热，也指炉子散出的温暖。

branches.en: BODY AND TONGUE: warmth becomes fever, then the burning of chilli.
branches.cn: 身体与舌头：热变成发热，再变成辣椒的灼烧。

branches.en: PEAK AND PRELIMINARY: feeling and sport both use heat for the stage that burns brightest.
branches.cn: 顶点与预赛：情绪与体育都用 heat 指烧得最旺的阶段。

branches.en: THE CAUSATIVE VERB: to heat is simply to put heat into something.
branches.cn: 使役动词：加热就是把热放进某物。

intro.en: Heat is a free English root that combines with particles and suffixes; the derived family is large and mostly transparent.
intro.cn: heat 是一个自由英语词根，可与小品词和后缀组合；派生词族庞大且大多一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; Latin calor and its family are semantic parallels only, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 calor 及其词族只是语义上的平行词，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Use a heatproof mat under the pan.

definition_en: to become aware of something one did not notice before; to make a plan or aim actually happen; to sell property and receive money for it
core_image: 走到半路忽然停住、回头的神情
scene: 走到半路，忽然想起钥匙还在桌上，脚步猛地停住。 She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
sceneCN: 这里 realize 是「意识到」（第 1 个义项：忽然明白某事）；句意为她忽然意识到门没锁。画面里可留意：停住的脚步、回头的神情、头顶亮起的灯。

derivatives.zh: realize 的词根，指真实的
real 加 -ity，指现实
realize 加 -ation，指认识、实现
un- 与 realized 复合，指未实现的

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become aware of something that was not noticed or understood before
senses.definitionCN: 察觉此前未注意或未理解之事
senses.example: She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 她忽然意识到门没锁。
senses.why: To realize is to make something real in the mind, to bring a fact into awareness where it was not before.
senses.whyCN: to realize 就是在心里使某物变为真实，把事实带到此前没有的觉察之中。

senses.title: To make happen
senses.definition: to turn a plan, aim or hope into actual fact
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、目标或希望变成实际事实
senses.example: He worked hard to realize his dream of opening a shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他努力工作以实现开一家店的梦想。
senses.why: The other direction of the same image is to make a thing real in the world, not only in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象的另一方向，是使某物在世界上真实存在，而不只在心里。

senses.title: To sell for money
senses.definition: to sell property or goods and receive money for them
senses.definitionCN: 卖掉财产或货物并换成钱
senses.example: The company realized a large sum from the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 公司从事这笔买卖中获得了一大笔钱。
senses.why: Property sold becomes money actually in hand, so the word took on the commercial sense of turning an asset into cash.
senses.whyCN: 售出的财产变成手里实实在在的钱，于是这个词有了「把资产换成现金」的商业义。

intro.en: Realize is real plus the verb ending -ize, modelled on Latin realis; it means to make real, whether in the mind or in the world.
intro.cn: realize 是 real 加动词词尾 -ize，仿拉丁语 realis 构成；意为「使真实」，无论在心中还是在世上。

items.en: Res meant a thing, and what is real is what belongs to things as they exist.
items.cn: res 意为事物，而真实之物就是属于实际存在之物的东西。

items.en: Realis meant belonging to a thing, and English real grew from it.
items.cn: realis 意为属于事物的，英语 real 由它而来。

items.en: The ending -ize forms verbs meaning to make or become, so real plus -ize is to make real.
items.cn: 词尾 -ize 构成意为「使……成为」的动词，因此 real 加 -ize 就是「使真实」。

items.en: One can make a fact real to the mind by realizing it, or make a plan real in the world by carrying it out.
items.cn: 人可以通过 realize 使事实在心智中变真，也可以通过执行使计划在世界上成真。

items.en: Modern English uses realize for awareness, for the completion of plans, and for turning property into money.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realize 指觉察、完成计划，以及把财产换成钱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of noticing, achieving and selling.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示察觉、达成与出售的动词。

entries.definition: Actually existing.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在的。

entries.definition: The state of being real.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的状态。

entries.definition: Close to real life.
entries.definitionCN: 贴近现实生活的。

entries.definition: The act of becoming aware or making real.
entries.definitionCN: 认识或实现的行为。

entries.definition: To see or become aware of.

entries.definition: To grasp the meaning of.

entries.definition: To reach a goal by effort.

entries.definition: To carry out a promise or aim.

normalIntro.en: The verb has two directions: making something real in the mind, which is awareness, and making it real in the world, which is achievement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词有两个方向：在心里使某物变真，即觉察；在世上使某物成真，即实现。

normal.en: Realize is real plus -ize, so it means to make real.
normal.cn: realize 是 real 加 -ize，意为「使真实」。

normal.en: To realize a fact is to make it real to your mind.
normal.cn: to realize 一个事实，就是让它在你心里变真。

normal.en: To realize a plan is to make it real in the world.
normal.cn: to realize 一个计划，就是让它在世上成真。

normal.en: Realize an asset is to turn property into money you can hold.
normal.cn: realize 一项资产，就是把财产变成手里能拿的钱。

normal.en: Realization is the noun, naming either the moment of awareness or the completion of a plan.
normal.cn: realization 是名词，或指觉察的那一刻，或指计划的完成。

abstract.en: We often realize too late what we already knew.
abstract.cn: 我们常常太晚才 realize 早已知道的事。

abstract.en: A dream realized changes the person who dreamed it.
abstract.cn: 被实现的梦想会改变做梦的人。

abstract.en: Awareness and achievement share one word because both make the invisible real.
abstract.cn: 觉察与成就共用一个词，因为两者都让看不见的变真。

examples.en: She suddenly realized that the door was unlocked.
examples.cn: 她忽然意识到门没锁。

examples.en: He worked hard to realize his dream of opening a shop.
examples.cn: 他努力工作以实现开一家店的梦想。

examples.en: The company realized a large sum from the sale.
examples.cn: 公司从事这笔买卖中获得了一大笔钱。

definition_en: one more of the same kind, or a different one, or each other
core_image: 桌上已经有一只杯子，又摆上另一只同样的杯子
scene: 桌上已经有一只杯子，有人又摆上一只同样的杯子。 Would you like another cup of tea?

senses.title: One more of the same kind
senses.definition: one more person or thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类的人或物再增加一个
senses.example: Would you like another cup of tea?
senses.exampleCN: 你要再来一杯茶吗？
senses.why: An plus other puts one more item beside the first, so the added item is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: an 加 other 把又一件东西放在第一件旁边，所以新增的那件就是第一义。

senses.title: A different one
senses.definition: a different one, not the one already named
senses.definitionCN: 与已经提到的那个不同的一个
senses.example: That is another question altogether.
senses.exampleCN: 那完全是另一个问题。
senses.why: Other also marks difference, so the word can point to a thing of a separate kind.
senses.whyCN: other 也标记差异，所以这个词也能指向另一类的事物。

senses.title: Each other
senses.definition: each other, used in the fixed phrase one another
senses.definitionCN: 互相，用于固定短语 one another
senses.example: They help one another after class.
senses.exampleCN: 他们课后互相帮助。
senses.why: When the two sides act on each other, the pair is pictured as one and the other.
senses.whyCN: 当双方作用于对方，这一对就被画成「一个与另一个」。

senses.title: To behave towards someone
senses.definition: to behave in a particular way towards a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式对待人或物
senses.example: She treats her students as equals.
senses.exampleCN: 她把学生当平等的人看待。

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tractare 意为「处理、摆弄」，你怎么摆弄人，就是怎么对待人。

senses.title: To give medical care
senses.definition: to give medical care to a sick or injured person
senses.definitionCN: 对病人或伤者施以医疗
senses.example: The doctor treated him for a broken wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给他治腕骨骨折。
senses.why: Medicine is a special kind of handling, so the same verb takes on the clinic.
senses.whyCN: 医疗是处理的一种特别方式，于是同一个动词走进了诊室。

senses.title: To deal with a substance
senses.definition: to apply a process to a material so that it changes
senses.definitionCN: 对材料施加某种工序使其改变
senses.example: The wood is treated against rot.
senses.exampleCN: 这木材经过防腐处理。
senses.why: Handling a material with a chemical is literally a handling, and the verb fits.
senses.whyCN: 用化学品去处理材料，字面上就是「摆弄」，动词正合适。

senses.title: To give food or fun at your cost
senses.definition: to buy food or entertainment for someone as a gift
senses.definitionCN: 花钱请别人吃东西或娱乐
senses.example: He treated us to lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他请我们吃了午饭。
senses.why: Handling someone generously in a social setting becomes paying for them.
senses.whyCN: 在社交场合大方地「对付」某人，就变成了替他们付钱。

senses.title: A gift or pleasure given
senses.definition: something enjoyable given as a gift, or a special pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 作为礼物给人的享受，或特别的乐事
senses.example: The trip was a real treat.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行真是难得的乐事。
senses.why: The noun keeps the sense of something generously handled and then given.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「被大方地打理好然后送给人」的含义。

senses.title: To discuss or write about
senses.definition: to deal with a subject in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 以口头或书面方式讨论一个主题
senses.example: The book treats the subject briefly.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对这个问题论述简略。
senses.why: Tractare also meant to discuss, the sense that survives in treatise and treaty.
senses.whyCN: tractare 也有「讨论」义，这层意思留在 treatise 与 treaty 里。

intro.en: The verb comes from Old French traitier, from Latin tractare, to handle or discuss.
intro.cn: 这个动词来自古法语 traitier，源头是拉丁语 tractare（处理、讨论）。

items.en: Trahere means to draw or pull, and tractare is its frequentative, to keep handling.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉，tractare 是它的反复形式，意为反复摆弄。

items.en: Traitier means to deal with a person, to negotiate, or to discuss a matter.
items.cn: 古法语 traitier 意为与人打交道、谈判或讨论某事。

items.en: English takes the verb for behaving towards people and for handling subjects.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，用于待人与论述主题。

items.en: Medicine turns handling into healing, and hospitality turns it into paying.
items.cn: 医学把「处理」变成治疗，好客把「处理」变成付钱。

items.en: The noun treat, a pleasure, appears much later than the verb.
items.cn: 名词 treat（乐事）比动词晚得多才出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of dealing with people or illness.
note.cn: 形近组共用 tract- 词干，近义组汇集表示待人、治病的其他动词。

entries.definition: the way someone is dealt with, or cured

entries.definition: a long written work on a subject

entries.definition: to ask someone earnestly

entries.definition: to make a sick person well again

normalIntro.en: Treat, treaty, treatise and treatment all grow from one Latin verb of handling.
normalIntro.cn: treat、treaty、treatise、treatment 都出自同一个表示「处理」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Tractare is to handle, so treat is to handle a person, a wound, or a subject.
normal.cn: tractare 是处理，所以 treat 是处理一个人、一处伤或一个题目。

normal.en: Treatment is the noun: how someone or something is handled.
normal.cn: treatment 是名词：某人或某物被怎样处理。

normal.en: A treaty is a handling written down between states.
normal.cn: treaty 是国家之间写下来的「处理」。

normal.en: My treat means I pay, the handling made generous.
normal.cn: my treat 是我付钱，把「处理」变成了大方。

normal.en: The past is treated, and the door of the clinic uses the same word.
normal.cn: 过去式是 treated，诊所门上用的也是这个词。

abstract.en: Picture an adult bending to a child’s height before speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象大人弯到孩子的高度再开口。

abstract.en: The same bend is made over a wound, and over a hard material.
abstract.cn: 同一个弯腰，对着伤口，也对着硬材料。

abstract.en: Then see a hand reaching for the bill at dinner.
abstract.cn: 再看见饭后一只手去拿账单。

examples.en: They treated the old man with great respect.
examples.cn: 他们非常敬重这位老人。

examples.en: The nurse treated the cut and sent him home.
examples.cn: 护士处理了伤口就送他回家了。

examples.en: Let me treat you to a coffee.
examples.cn: 让我请你喝杯咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹特」——特别热情地吹一气，好好招待客人。

sensesIntro.en: All senses are ways of handling something: a person, a wound, a material, a subject, or a bill.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都是「处理」：处理一个人、一处伤、一种材料、一个题目，或一笔账。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an adult bending down to a child’s eye level.
core.cn: 核心意象：大人蹲到与孩子齐眼的高度。

branches.en: The social sense, how one person handles another.
branches.cn: 人际义：一个人怎样对待另一个人。

branches.en: The technical senses: handling a body or a material.
branches.cn: 技术义：处理身体或处理材料。

branches.en: The generous senses: paying, and the pleasure paid for.
branches.cn: 慷慨义：付钱，以及花钱买来的乐事。

branches.en: The written sense, kept alive in treatise and treaty.
branches.cn: 书面义：活在 treatise 与 treaty 里。

branches.en: The material sense, where timber is the thing handled.
branches.cn: 材料义：被处理的是木料。

intro.en: The verb is a worn-down Latin verb of handling, and its family is large.
intro.cn: 这个动词是磨圆了的拉丁语「处理」动词，词族很大。

latinIntro.en: The tract- stem appears in treat, treaty, treatment, tract, contract, and extract.
latinIntro.cn: tract- 词干出现在 treat、treaty、treatment、tract、contract 与 extract 里。

items.example: The stem gives tract and contract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tract 与 contract。

items.meaning: to handle a person or thing

items.example: The treaty was signed in May.

items.meaning: a written handling of a subject
items.example: She wrote a treatise on bees.

definition_zh: 管理；经营；（企业的）管理层；对疾病或局面的处理方式
definition_en: the activity of running and controlling an organization or process, or the people who do it
core_image: 一只手把散在各处的线头收拢，编成一股能拉动的缰绳
scene: 四家分店各做各的账，月底总对不上数，后来同一个人统一排班、定采购、查库存。 Careful management brought the four branches onto one schedule.
sceneCN: 这里 management 指把分散的人、钱与流程收在一起加以调度（第 1 个义项：对组织的统筹经营）；句意：细致的管理让四家分店归到同一张时间表上。图中可辨识物件：账本、排班表、货箱、统一的门牌。

senses.title: Running an organization
senses.titleCN: 把一个组织的各项工作统筹起来
senses.definition: the activity of planning, organizing and controlling the work of an organization so that it runs well
senses.definitionCN: 对一个组织的各项工作加以计划、组织与控制，使其运转良好
senses.example: Good management kept the shipyard busy through the downturn.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的管理让这家船厂在衰退期仍有活干。
senses.why: The word began as handling a horse with the hand, and running a firm is that same gesture applied to people, money and schedules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指用手摆弄、驯服一匹马；经营一家公司，就是把同样的动作施加到人、钱与日程上。

senses.title: The people in charge
senses.definition: the group of senior people who make the main decisions in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织里作出主要决策的高层群体
senses.example: Management agreed to freeze hiring until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 管理层同意把招聘冻结到春天。
senses.why: Once the activity became a permanent job, the people who did it could be spoken of as one body.
senses.whyCN: 当这种活计变成常设职位，做这件事的人就被当作一个整体来说。

senses.title: Skill in handling people
senses.definition: the ability to deal with people and awkward situations without letting them get out of hand
senses.definitionCN: 与人以及棘手局面打交道时不让事情失控的能力
senses.example: It took patient management to keep the two departments speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 要让两个部门继续对话，需要很有耐心的周旋。
senses.why: A rider controls a horse by feel rather than force, and the same word covers handling people by feel.
senses.whyCN: 骑手靠手感而不是蛮力控制马匹，这个词也用来指靠分寸感与人相处。

senses.title: Careful use of resources
senses.titleCN: 对钱财与时间的节制使用
senses.definition: the careful control of money, time or supplies so that nothing is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 对金钱、时间或物资的谨慎支配，使什么也不被浪费
senses.example: Tighter management of the fuel budget halved the depot's winter costs.
senses.exampleCN: 对燃料预算更严格的把控让仓库的冬季开支减半。
senses.why: What the hand holds it can also ration; the horse-training word grew into the sense of not letting a supply run out.
senses.whyCN: 手握得住东西，也就能分配它；驯马那个词由此长出「不让储备用尽」的意思。

senses.title: Medical care over time
senses.titleCN: 对慢性病的长期治疗与监控
senses.definition: the treatment and steady control of a disease or condition, especially one that lasts
senses.definitionCN: 对疾病或身体状况进行治疗与持续控制，尤指长期存在的情况
senses.example: Pain management now includes a weekly check with a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛管理现在包含每周由护士做的一次复查。
senses.why: A doctor who keeps a disease in hand for months is managing it in the same old sense of handling.
senses.whyCN: 医生把一种病在手里管上几个月，用的仍是「用手把控」那个老意思。

senses.title: Control of land and animals
senses.titleCN: 对土地、畜群等自然资源的经营
senses.definition: the control and use of land, animals or natural resources according to a plan
senses.definitionCN: 按计划对土地、牲畜或自然资源加以控制与使用
senses.example: The ranch's grazing management keeps the grass from wearing out.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场的放牧管理让草场不至于被耗尽。
senses.why: Herds and fields were the first things a hand had to manage, so land and livestock keep the oldest layer of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 畜群与田地是手最早要照管的对象，因此土地与牲畜保留了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: Management as a subject
senses.titleCN: 作为一门学科的管理学
senses.definition: the study of how organizations are run, taught as an academic subject
senses.definitionCN: 研究组织如何运转的学问，作为一门学科来教授
senses.example: He added a management course to his engineering degree.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工程学位之外又加了一门管理课程。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the handling of firms was written down, taught and examined, and so became a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 到了二十世纪，经营企业的门道被写成教材、被教授、被考试，于是成了一门学问。

senses.title: The handling of an event
senses.titleCN: 对某一具体事件或局面的处置
senses.definition: the way a particular problem, crisis or event is dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 对某个具体问题、危机或事件的应对方式
senses.example: The management of the flood response drew criticism from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水应对的处置方式招来了居民的批评。
senses.why: Here the object of handling shrinks from a whole firm to one event, but the gesture itself stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里被把控的对象从整个公司缩小到一桩事件，动作本身没有变。

intro.en: Management is the noun of manage, which came through Italian from Latin manus 'hand'. The modern business sense grew out of handling horses, then households, then firms.
intro.cn: management 是 manage 的名词，而 manage 经意大利语上溯到拉丁 manus「手」；现代企业义由驯马、理家一路扩展到经营公司。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand' and also the power to hold something under control, so handling and controlling were one idea from the start.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」，也指把某物握在控制之下的权力，因此「用手摆弄」与「掌控」从一开始就是一个念头。

items.en: Italian maneggiare, built on mano 'hand', meant to handle an object and especially to train a horse; the horse sense is the one usually cited for the English verb.
items.cn: 意大利语 maneggiare 由 mano「手」构成，指用手操作物件，尤指驯马；英语动词最常被追溯到的是驯马这一义。

items.en: Manage entered English in the sixteenth century, first of handling horses and weapons; management, the noun of the activity, followed in the same period.
items.cn: manage 在十六世纪进入英语，最初用于摆弄马匹与兵器；指这项活动的名词 management 也在同一时期出现。

items.en: French ménager 'to run a household' is generally thought to have strengthened the sense of ordering a household or estate, which later widened to a business.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 ménager「料理家务」强化了「安排家务与产业」这一义，后来再扩大到经营企业。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum through French, names the activity or its result, which is how management came to mean both the doing and the body that does it.
items.cn: 这个名词后缀经法语来自拉丁语中表示动作或结果的后缀，management 因此既指「做这件事」，也指「做这件事的那群人」。

items.en: The first recorded dates for the business and academic senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 企业义与学科义的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十六世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like management; the second group names neighbouring ways of running something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 management 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「经营、支配」说法。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; it keeps the plain action of handling a firm or a horse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，保留「摆弄、经营一家公司或一匹马」的直白动作。

entries.definition: The person who performs the activity, formed with the agent suffix; it is not the activity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做这件事的人，由施动后缀构成，不是这项活动本身。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything connected with managers or their methods.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述与管理者或管理方法有关的事物。

entries.definition: A riding school, from the same Italian word for handling horses; the link is the stable, not the office.
entries.definitionCN: 指马术学校，同出那个表示驯马的意大利词；联系在马厩，而不在办公室。

entries.definition: From Latin manica 'sleeve, handcuff', also built on manus, but it names a restraint rather than a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 manica「袖子、手铐」，同样由 manus 构成，但指束缚之物，不是经营的本事。

entries.definition: The running of an institution according to its rules; it stresses procedure more than direction.
entries.definitionCN: 按规章维持机构运转，强调程序多过掌舵。

entries.definition: The system by which an organization is directed and held accountable, rather than the daily work of running it.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织被引导并接受问责的制度，而非日常经营的具体事务。

entries.definition: Careful, responsible handling of money or resources left in one's charge.
entries.definitionCN: 对受托的钱财资源做审慎负责的照管。

entries.definition: Authority to direct something; it names the power, while management names the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 支配某事的权力；它指权力本身，management 指整套活动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Manus is Latin for hand, so management is literally handling.
normal.cn: manus 是拉丁语「手」，management 字面上就是「用手摆弄、照管」。

normal.en: The family runs manage, manager, managerial, manageable and mismanagement.
normal.cn: 同族词有 manage、manager、managerial、manageable 与 mismanagement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: time management, crisis management, top management.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：时间管理、危机处理、高层管理层。

normal.en: The noun suffix -ment turns the act of managing into the thing called management.
normal.cn: 名词后缀把「管理」这个动作变成名为 management 的事物。

normal.en: Italian maneggiare first meant to train a horse by hand, which is the oldest picture in the word.
normal.cn: 意大利语 maneggiare 最初指用手驯马，这是这个词里最古老的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on four loose threads at once and pulling them into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一次攥住四根散线，把它们拉成一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a rider who never pulls hard, only shifts weight, and the whole herd follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不猛拉缰绳、只挪动重心的骑手，整群马都跟着走。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where every paper is already filed before anyone asks for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，别人还没开口要，每份纸就已经归好了位。

examples.en: Local clinics improved their management of patient records last year.
examples.cn: 本地诊所去年改善了对病人档案的管理。

examples.en: The management of the harbour was split between two agencies.
examples.cn: 港口的经营权被分给了两个机构。

examples.en: She studied management after six years on the factory floor.
examples.cn: 在车间干了六年后，她去攻读管理学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「man（人）+ age（年纪）+ ment（名词）」——管人管到上年纪，就是管理

root: 拉丁 manus「手」→ 意大利 maneggiare「用手操作、驯马」→ 法语 ménager「料理家务」→ 英语 manage「管理」；末尾是名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand: it runs a firm, becomes a body of managers, handles people, rations supplies, holds a disease in check, works land and herds, turns into a taught subject, and finally grips a single event.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一只手：经营一家公司、聚成一群管理者、应对人、分配物资、把病管住、照料土地与畜群、变成一门被教授的学问，最后攥住一桩具体事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand gathers loose threads and pulls them into a single rein.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把散开的线头收拢，拉成一根缰绳。

branches.en: THE HAND ITSELF: planning, organizing and controlling a whole firm is the original gesture at full size.
branches.cn: 手本身：对一个公司作计划、组织与控制，就是最初那个动作放到最大。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS THE REIN: the handlers become a standing body, and their feel for people becomes a skill.
branches.cn: 谁握着缰绳：做事的人聚成常设群体，他们待人的手感变成一种本事。

branches.en: WHAT IS RATIONED: the hand decides how much fuel, time or money may leave the store.
branches.cn: 被分配的东西：手决定有多少燃料、时间或钱可以从库里出去。

branches.en: CARE OVER TIME: a disease and a pasture are both kept in condition by regular attention.
branches.cn: 长期的照料：疾病与牧场都靠按时看顾才维持在可用状态。

branches.en: FROM PRACTICE TO OBJECT: the habit is written down as a subject, or narrowed to one event.
branches.cn: 从做法变成对象：这套习惯被写成学科，或被收窄到一桩事件上。

intro.en: Management is built from a Latin hand and a noun suffix, and the hand also supports several English words.
intro.cn: management 由一个拉丁语「手」和一个名词后缀构成，这个「手」还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manacle and mandate; the Italian verb maneggiare gives manage and its English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manus 衍生 manual（手册）、manacle（手铐）与 mandate（委托）；意大利语 maneggiare 衍生 manage 及其英语词族。

items.example: The root supplies the picture of a hand on a rein.

definition_zh: 呼吸；一口气；口气、呼出的气；一丝微风；顺畅呼吸的状态
definition_en: an amount of air taken into the lungs, the air that comes out of the mouth, a very slight movement of air, or the state of breathing easily
core_image: 口鼻前呼出的一团淡淡白气
scene: 跑完步，他站在跑道边弯下腰，想喘匀这口气。 After the race he stood by the track, trying to catch his breath.
sceneCN: 这里 breath 是「呼吸；一口气」（第 1 个义项：吸入又呼出的一股空气）；句意为跑完步后他站在跑道边，想把这口气喘匀。

pos.zh: 名词：呼吸；一口气；口气；一丝微风

derivatives.zh: 与 breath 同源，义为「呼吸」
由 breathe 加 -ing 构成，义为「呼吸；呼吸动作」
由 breath 加 -less 构成，义为「喘不上气的；屏息的」
由 breath 与 taking 组合而成，义为「令人惊叹的；惊险的」

senses.title: One amount of air taken in
senses.definition: an amount of air taken into the lungs and then let out
senses.definitionCN: 吸入肺里再呼出的一股空气
senses.example: He took a deep breath before he jumped.
senses.exampleCN: 他跳之前深吸了一口气。
senses.why: Old English braeth first meant vapour or smell, the mist that leaves the mouth, and the air taken in took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 braeth 最初指蒸气或气味，也就是离开嘴边的雾气，吸入的空气也沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: The air that comes out
senses.definition: the air that comes out of your mouth, especially when it has a smell
senses.definitionCN: 从嘴里呼出的气，尤指带气味时
senses.example: Onions can give you bad breath.
senses.exampleCN: 吃洋葱会让人有口臭。
senses.why: What leaves the body as vapour became the everyday word for the smell of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 以蒸气形式离开身体的东西，后来成了日常指口腔气味的词。

senses.title: A slight movement of air
senses.definition: a very small amount of wind or moving air
senses.definitionCN: 极少量流动的空气或风
senses.example: Not a breath of wind moved the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一丝风也没有，树叶纹丝不动。
senses.why: A small puff of air looks like a single breath, so the word named the faintest wind.
senses.whyCN: 一小股空气看起来就像呼出的一口气，于是这个词也用来指最轻微的风。

senses.title: The state of breathing easily
senses.definition: the state of being able to breathe easily, chiefly in phrases such as out of breath
senses.definitionCN: 能够轻松呼吸的状态，主要用于 out of breath 这类短语
senses.example: The long climb left him out of breath.
senses.exampleCN: 那段长长的攀爬让他上气不接下气。
senses.why: The word for the air also names the easy flow of that air; when the flow stops, a person is out of breath.
senses.whyCN: 指空气的词也用来指空气顺畅的流动；流动一断，人就上气不接下气。

intro.en: Breath began as a word for vapour and smell, then narrowed to the air a person breathes.
intro.cn: breath 最初指蒸气与气味，后来缩小为一个人呼吸的空气。

items.en: Braeth meant vapour, smell or the mist of the mouth.
items.cn: braeth 意为蒸气、气味或口中的雾气。

items.en: German Brodem and Dutch braam carry a nearby sense of steam or smell.
items.cn: 德语 Brodem 与荷兰语 braam 都带有蒸气或气味的意思。

items.en: The word narrowed to the air a living body takes in and sends out.
items.cn: 这个词缩小为活着的身体吸入与呼出的空气。

items.en: Breath kept this sense, while the verb breathe grew beside it.
items.cn: breath 保留了这一义项，动词 breathe 在它旁边发展出来。

items.en: Today breath also names a faint wind and the easy flow of air in the body.
items.cn: 今天 breath 还指微弱的风，以及体内空气的顺畅流动。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about air and breathing.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与空气、呼吸有关的词。

entries.definition: The verb that means to take air in and out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼吸」，与 breath 同源。

entries.definition: The distance from one side to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宽度」，拼写与 breath 相近。

entries.definition: A gap made in a wall or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺口；违反」，读音与 breath 接近。

entries.definition: The mixture of gases that living things breathe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空气」。

entries.definition: Air moving across the land.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风」。

entries.definition: A short burst of air or smoke.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一小股气或烟」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English braeth meant vapour, and the mist of the mouth is still the picture behind it.
normal.cn: 古英语 braeth 意为蒸气，口中的雾气至今仍是它背后的画面。

normal.en: The word then narrowed to the air a body takes in and sends out.
normal.cn: 这个词随后缩小为身体吸入与呼出的空气。

normal.en: A tiny puff of air looks like one breath, so a faint wind is a breath of wind.
normal.cn: 一小股空气就像一口气，所以微弱的风叫作 a breath of wind。

normal.en: It often pairs with deep, out of, bad and hold.
normal.cn: 它常与 deep、out of、bad、hold 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-e-a-t-h; it is the noun, while breathe is the verb.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-e-a-t-h，它是名词，动词则是 breathe。

abstract.en: See a faint white cloud leave a mouth on a cold morning: that cloud is breath.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷的清晨，嘴边飘出一小团白气：那团白气就是 breath。

abstract.en: Thin that cloud until it barely moves a leaf and it becomes a breath of wind.
abstract.cn: 把这团白气稀释到几乎吹不动一片叶子，它就变成了「一丝微风」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the white cloud bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那团白气把意思带回来。

examples.en: He took a deep breath before he jumped.
examples.cn: 他跳之前深吸了一口气。

examples.en: Onions can give you bad breath.
examples.cn: 吃洋葱会让人有口臭。

examples.en: The long climb left him out of breath.
examples.cn: 那段长长的攀爬让他上气不接下气。

root: breath 在古英语中写作 braeth，意为蒸气、气味或口中的雾气，与德语 Brodem、荷兰语 braam 有相近的含义。后来词义缩小为活着的身体吸入与呼出的空气，动词 breathe 也在它旁边发展出来。今天 breath 指一次呼吸、呼出的口气、一丝微风，以及顺畅呼吸的状态。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of breath grow from one picture: a faint cloud of air leaving the mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: breath 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：从嘴边飘出的一小团淡淡白气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faint cloud of air in front of the mouth
core.cn: 核心意象：口鼻前呼出的一小团淡淡白气

branches.en: THE INTAKE: one amount of air taken in and let out.
branches.cn: 吸气线：吸入又呼出的一股空气。

branches.en: THE EXHALE: the air leaving the mouth and its smell.
branches.cn: 呼气线：离开嘴边的空气及它的气味。

branches.en: THE BREEZE: a puff of air too small to be called wind.
branches.cn: 微风线：小到称不上风的一股空气。

branches.en: THE FLOW: breathing easily or losing that ease.
branches.cn: 流动线：呼吸顺畅，或失去这份顺畅。

branches.en: THE CLOUD: air going in and air coming out share one visible mist.
branches.cn: 白气线：吸入与呼出的空气共享同一团可见的雾气。

intro.cn: breath 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin spiritus means breath and spirit; it is a parallel word, not the source of breath.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus 意为「呼吸；气息」，它是平行词，不是 breath 的来源。

items.example: Braeth is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: braeth 是有记录的古英语形式。

items.example: It forms take a deep breath.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 take a deep breath。

items.example: It forms a breath of wind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 a breath of wind。

definition_zh: 舒服的；舒适的；安逸的；宽裕的
definition_en: making you feel relaxed and free of pain; having enough money for a good life
core_image: 陷进软沙发里的那种放松感
scene: 上完一整天体育课回到家，我换上拖鞋瘫进了大沙发。 Of all the seats in our house, this old sofa is truly comfortable.
sceneCN: 这里 comfortable 是「舒服的」（第 1 个义项：身体放松、不难受）；句意是这张旧沙发是家里最舒服的座位。

derivatives.zh: 由词根 comfort 加名词后缀构成，义为「舒适；安慰」
由 comfortable 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「舒服地」
由否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不舒服的；不自在的」
由 comfort 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人安慰的」

senses.title: Pleasant to sit in, wear or touch
senses.definition: making you feel relaxed because it is soft and easy on the body
senses.definitionCN: 让人放松，因为柔软、贴身不难受
senses.example: These running shoes are very comfortable for long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这双跑鞋走长路很舒服。
senses.why: The core image is sinking into something soft, so anything soft and easy on the body earns this word.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是陷进柔软的东西里，所以凡是让身体放松不费劲的东西都可以用它形容。

senses.title: Feeling relaxed and not worried
senses.definition: feeling calm and free from worry or embarrassment in a place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地方或场合感到平静，不担心、不尴尬
senses.example: I did not feel comfortable answering questions in front of the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 在全班面前回答问题让我很不自在。
senses.why: When the body relaxes, the mind often follows, so the word stretched from physical ease to emotional ease.
senses.whyCN: 身体放松时心情往往也跟着放松，所以这个词从身体上的舒适延伸到了心理上的自在。

senses.title: Having enough money without worry
senses.definition: having enough money to live well without financial problems
senses.definitionCN: 钱够用，生活没有经济压力
senses.example: Her grandparents live a comfortable life in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母在小镇上过着宽裕的生活。
senses.why: A life free of hardship feels like a soft chair for the whole family, so the image of ease grew into wealth.
senses.whyCN: 没有艰辛的生活就像全家人坐上了软椅子，所以「安逸」的意象延伸成了「宽裕」。

intro.en: Comfortable traces back to a Latin verb that meant to strengthen greatly.
intro.cn: comfortable 可以追溯到拉丁语动词，本义是「大大加强」。

items.en: The Latin verb confortare meant to strengthen much, built on com- (intensive) and fortis (strong).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 confortare 意为大大加强，由加强语气的 com- 加 fortis（强壮的）构成。

items.en: Old French carried it over as conforter, meaning to comfort or console.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 conforter，意为安慰、抚慰。

items.en: English took comfort in the thirteenth century, first meaning strengthening or aid.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪吸收 comfort，最初指支持、帮助。

items.en: The adjective comfortable followed, at first meaning strengthening or cheering, then pleasant to the body.
items.cn: 形容词 comfortable 随之出现，起初指鼓舞人心的，后来指身体上舒服的。

items.en: Today comfortable covers soft chairs, easy feelings and a secure income.
items.cn: 如今 comfortable 可以形容软椅子、轻松的心情，也形容安稳的收入。

note.en: These words belong to the comfort family or describe pleasant, relaxed feelings.
note.cn: 这些词属于 comfort 词族，或同样描述轻松愉悦的感受。

entries.definitionCN: 温暖舒适的

entries.definition: British spelling of cozy
entries.definitionCN: cozy 的英式拼法

entries.definition: not worried or stiff
entries.definitionCN: 放松的

entries.definitionCN: 自在的；不紧张的

entries.definition: not hard to touch
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的

normalIntro.cn: 用 comfort 词族和身边的物件把拼写记牢。

normal.en: comfort + able = comfortable: able to give comfort.
normal.cn: comfort（舒适）+ able（能够的）＝让人能够感到舒适的东西。

normal.en: Note the hidden for: com-for-table, not comfrot.
normal.cn: 注意中间藏着 for：com-for-table，别拼成 comfrot。

normal.en: The opposite adds un-: uncomfortable.
normal.cn: 反义词加 un-：uncomfortable（不舒服）。

normal.en: The adverb swaps -able for -ably: comfortably.
normal.cn: 副词把 -able 换成 -ably：comfortably。

normal.en: Pronunciation shortcut: UK speech often hides the second syllable, KUMF-tuh-bl.
normal.cn: 发音捷径：英式口语常吞掉一个音节，读成 KUMF-tuh-bl。

abstract.en: Picture sinking into a giant pillow after school; nothing hurts, nothing presses.
abstract.cn: 想象放学后陷进一个巨大的枕头里，哪儿都不疼、哪儿都不压。

abstract.en: Feel the ease of a warm sweater on a cold day; that ease is the word.
abstract.cn: 感受冷天里套上暖毛衣的那种轻松感，这种轻松就是这个词。

abstract.en: A family with savings sits calmly at dinner; no worry, so a comfortable life.
abstract.cn: 有积蓄的一家人安静地吃饭，没有烦恼，这就是宽裕的生活。

examples.en: My new school shoes are more comfortable than the old ones.
examples.cn: 我的新校鞋比旧的那双舒服。

examples.en: Please make yourselves comfortable while we wait for the teacher.
examples.cn: 等老师的时候大家别拘束。

examples.en: It is warm today, so the scarf feels uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 今天很暖和，戴围巾觉得不自在。

sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从柔软的物件，到轻松的心情，再到安稳宽裕的生活。

core.cn: 核心意象：陷进柔软安全的东西里

branches.en: Soft chairs, shoes and beds
branches.cn: 软椅子、鞋子和床带来的舒服

core_image: 喉咙里发痒，一口气猛地冲出来，咳咳两声
scene: 秋游吹了冷风，小明一路轻咳。 He kept coughing on the windy bus home.
sceneCN: 这里 cough 是「咳嗽」（第 1 个义项：喉咙突然排气）；句意是回程车上风大，他一直咳嗽。

senses.title: To push air out of the throat suddenly
senses.definition: to force air out of the lungs with a sudden loud sound
senses.definitionCN: 以突发的响声把空气从肺部排出
senses.example: Cover your mouth when you cough in class.
senses.exampleCN: 在教室咳嗽时要捂住嘴。
senses.why: The throat clears itself with a burst of air, the body's quick sweep.
senses.whyCN: 喉咙以一股急气自我清扫，这是身体的快速打扫。

senses.title: To force something out of the throat
senses.definition: to bring something up from the throat or chest by coughing
senses.definitionCN: 通过咳嗽把东西从喉咙或胸口排出
senses.example: He coughed up the fish bone safely.
senses.exampleCN: 他安全地咳出了鱼刺。
senses.why: The burst of air can carry small trouble out of the chest.
senses.whyCN: 这股急气能把胸腔里的小麻烦带出来。

senses.title: An illness marked by coughing
senses.definition: an illness that makes you cough often
senses.definitionCN: 让人不断咳嗽的疾病
senses.example: A bad cough kept her home for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 严重的咳嗽让她在家休息了两天。
senses.why: The action names the sickness that repeats it.
senses.whyCN: 动作之名转指反复出现的病症。

intro.en: Cough is an English word that imitates the sound itself.
intro.cn: cough 是模仿咳嗽声的英语本土词。

items.en: The verb cohhet meant to cough, built from sound.
items.cn: 古英语动词 cohhet 意为咳嗽，源于拟声。

items.en: The word became coughen with Dutch kochen nearby.
items.cn: 中世纪英语变为 coughen，与荷兰语 kochen 并存。

items.en: Dutch hoesten kept a similar sound-based form.
items.cn: 荷兰语 hoesten 保留了相似的拟声形式。

items.en: The spelling settled as cough in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪拼法定为 cough。

items.en: Though spelled with gh, it is said like /kɒf/, echoing the sound.
items.cn: 虽拼作 gh，却读 /kɒf/，仍回响着咳嗽声。

definition_en: and not; used to join a second negative word or clause, especially after neither or not
core_image: 两扇门并排关着，左边一把锁，右边也一把锁
scene: 仓库两扇门都上了锁，左边一把，右边一把。 Neither the driver nor the guard saw the signal.
sceneCN: 这里 nor 是「也不」（第 1 个义项：与 neither 搭配，连接两个都被否定的选项）；句意是司机和警卫都没有看见信号。图中可辨识物件：两扇门、两把锁。

derivatives.zh: 与 nor 配对的否定连词，源自古英语 nāwðer，义为「两者都不」
中古英语形式，nor 的前身，义为「也不」
与 nor 出自同一个古英语词 hwæðer，义为「两者之一」

senses.title: Joining two denied alternatives after neither
senses.definition: used with neither to connect two words or phrases that are both denied
senses.definitionCN: 与 neither 搭配，连接两个都被否定的词或短语
senses.example: Neither the driver nor the guard saw the signal.
senses.exampleCN: 司机和警卫都没有看见信号。
senses.why: The word began as a compressed not either, so its central task is to add a second denied choice after the first has already been ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是「也不」的压缩说法，所以它的核心任务是在第一个选项已被排除之后，再补上一个同样被否定的选项。

senses.title: Adding a negative clause after not, with the verb inverted
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to add another negative clause, usually with the auxiliary before the subject
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定陈述之后，再补一个否定从句，通常把助动词提到主语前面
senses.example: She did not answer, nor did she look up.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有回答，也没有抬头。
senses.why: When two negative statements stand side by side, the second borrows this word, and English marks the link by putting the auxiliary first.
senses.whyCN: 当两个否定陈述并排时，第二个就借用这个词，英语再把助动词提到主语前，以标出这层连接。

senses.title: Literary double use, nor joined to nor
senses.titleCN: 也不……也不（书面重复用法）
senses.definition: used twice in formal or poetic writing to exclude two items with doubled emphasis, without neither
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或诗体文字里连用两次，以加倍的强调排除两个项目，而不借助 neither
senses.example: Nor food nor shelter did they give him.
senses.exampleCN: 他们既没给他食物，也没给他住处。
senses.why: Poets and older writers could repeat the word on both sides, doubling the denial for emphasis instead of leaning on neither.
senses.whyCN: 诗人和旧时作者会把这个词在两边各用一次，用重复来加强否定，而不必依赖 neither。

intro.en: Nor is a clipped Old English pronoun-conjunction meaning not either, reshaped in Middle English and fixed by the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: nor 是一个意为「也不」的古英语代词性连词削短而来，中古英语里经过改形，到十四世纪定形。

items.en: Nāwðer was built from nā, never or no, and hwæðer, which of two, and it meant not either of the two.
items.cn: nāwðer 由 nā（从不、不）与 hwæðer（两者中的哪一个）构成，意为「两者之中哪一个都不」。

items.en: Middle English shortened the word to nother, still meaning not either, and it was often paired with other negatives.
items.cn: 中古英语把词缩成 nother，仍表示「哪一个也不」，并常与其他否定词连用。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the written form nor appeared, generally explained as nother trimmed under the influence of or.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，书面形式 nor 出现，一般认为这是 nother 在 or 的影响下被削短的结果。

items.en: Nor spread first in paired constructions and then in clauses after a negative, while neither kept the fuller role.
items.cn: nor 先在成对结构里流行，随后用于否定句之后的从句，而 neither 保留了更完整的分工。

items.en: Modern English uses nor after neither, after not, and in literary double negatives, though everyday speech often prefers not either.
items.cn: 现代英语在 neither 之后、not 之后以及书面的双重否定里用 nor，不过日常口语常更爱说 not either。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the paired negative word, its older form and the alternative conjunction it is often set against; the near-meaning group collects plainer ways of adding a second denial.
note.cn: 形近组收与它配对的否定词、它的旧形式，以及常与它对照的选择连词；近义组收更朴素的「再加一层否定」说法。

entries.definition: The paired negative word that excludes both of two alternatives.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个选项一起排除的配对否定词。

entries.definition: An archaic form from which the shorter conjunction developed.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的形式，较短的连词由它发展而来。

entries.definition: The positive alternative conjunction, often used in the same sentence pattern, with a separate origin.
entries.definitionCN: 表示肯定选择的连词，常出现在同一类句型里，来源与此词不同。

entries.definition: The plain negative adverb used to deny a word or a clause.
entries.definitionCN: 用于否定一个词或一个从句的普通否定副词。

entries.definition: A phrase that adds a second denied item in ordinary speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中再补上一个被否定项的短语。

entries.definition: The everyday spoken way of adding a second negative.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中补上第二个否定项的常用说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a clipped form of a Germanic negative meaning not either, and its whole life has been spent arriving second.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「也不」的日耳曼语否定词的削短形式，它的一生都在充当第二个到场的否定。

normal.en: Nor is a trimmed form of an Old English word that meant not either of the two.
normal.cn: nor 是一个古英语词的削短形式，那词意为「两者中哪一个也不」。

normal.en: Neither keeps the paired frame, and nor supplies the second half of it.
normal.cn: neither 撑起成对的框架，nor 提供后半截。

normal.en: After not, the auxiliary moves in front of the subject, as in nor did she.
normal.cn: 在 not 之后，助动词移到主语前面，如 nor did she。

normal.en: The word is a conjunction, so it never takes an -s or an -ed ending.
normal.cn: 这个词是连词，所以从不加 -s 或 -ed 词尾。

normal.en: Everyday English often replaces it with not either, while formal writing keeps nor.
normal.cn: 日常英语常用 not either 代替它，正式书面语则保留 nor。

abstract.en: A word made by clipping two negatives into one shows how speech saves effort while keeping the denial.
abstract.cn: 一个把两重否定削成一个的词，说明口语如何在保留否定的同时省力。

abstract.en: Nor always arrives second, which is why it feels like an echo rather than a fresh claim.
abstract.cn: nor 总是第二个到场，所以它听起来像回声，而不像新的主张。

abstract.en: Its survival in formal prose is a small sign of how written English keeps structures that speech has already dropped.
abstract.cn: 它在正式散文里的存活，是书面英语保留口语早已丢掉的结构的微小迹象。

examples.en: Neither the driver nor the guard saw the signal.
examples.cn: 司机和警卫都没有看见信号。

examples.en: She did not answer, nor did she look up.
examples.cn: 她没有回答，也没有抬头。

examples.en: Nor food nor shelter did they give him.
examples.cn: 他们既没给他食物，也没给他住处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺」——点头应一声「诺」，也救不了两边都被否掉的事；记住 nor 是也不。

root: 古英语 nāwðer（nā「不」加 hwæðer「两者中哪一个」）经中古英语 nother 缩略，一般认为受 or 影响，在十四世纪定形为 nor。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a second denial; it divides into the neither pair, the inverted clause after not, and the doubled literary use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是第二层否定；由此分出与 neither 配对、否定句后的倒装从句，以及书面的重复用法。

core.cn: 核心意象：两扇门并排关着，各上各的锁。

branches.cn: 两扇锁着的门挡住同一位来客

branches.en: a list of two names, both crossed out
branches.cn: 两个名字都被划掉的名单

branches.cn: 既不回答也不抬头的证人

branches.cn: 既没摆盘也没放杯的桌子

branches.cn: 正式信里把拒绝写了两遍

latinIntro.en: The word was formed inside Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate, so no Latin source entry is recorded here.

definition_en: to guide or be in charge of others, to cause something to happen, or to be ahead
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，身后的人跟着他选的方向
scene: 队伍在岔路口停下，向导抬手示意大家往左边走。 She led the group through the narrow pass.
sceneCN: 这里是「带领、引导」（第 1 个义项：动词，指走在前头带路）；句意为她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。图中可辨识物件：岔路口、向导的手势、狭窄山口。

derivatives.zh: 由 lead 加 -er 构成，义为「领导者；领袖」
由 lead 加 -ing 构成，义为「领先的；主要的」
由 leader 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导；领导力」
由 mis-（错误地）加 lead 构成，义为「误导」

senses.title: To guide someone along a way
senses.definition: to go in front of others and show them the way
senses.definitionCN: 走在别人前面并为他们指路
senses.example: She led the group through the narrow pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to cause someone to go; the leader is the one who sets the direction of that going.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「使某人走」，带路的人就是决定「往哪走」的那个人。

senses.title: To be in charge of people or an activity
senses.definition: to direct a group, organization or activity and be responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一个群体、组织或活动并对其负责
senses.example: He leads a team of twelve engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 他领导着一支十二名工程师的团队。
senses.why: From physically going first it is a short step to deciding for others, so lead comes to mean holding authority.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上走在最前，很容易走到「替别人做决定」，于是 lead 转而指掌握权力。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to be the cause or route by which a result happens
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个结果发生的原因或路径
senses.example: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足可能导致严重的健康问题。
senses.why: A path leads to a place; events also have paths, so lead to names the route by which one thing brings about another.
senses.whyCN: 一条路通向一个地方；事情也有路径，所以 lead to 指一件事带出另一件事的路线。

senses.title: To be ahead in a race or competition
senses.definition: to have more points or be further forward than others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中比别人得分多或位置更靠前
senses.example: Our team leads by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队领先两球。
senses.why: The one in front is literally leading the line, and the racing sense keeps that simple picture of position.
senses.whyCN: 走在最前的人字面上就在「带」着队伍，竞赛义保留了这个简单的方位画面。

senses.title: The position of being ahead
senses.definition: the first place or advantage held over others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争中占据的第一名次或优势
senses.example: The champion held the lead until the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军一直保持领先直到最后一圈。
senses.why: The verb's sense of being in front turns into a noun naming that front position.
senses.whyCN: 动词「处在前面」的意思转成一个名词，指那个靠前的位置。

senses.title: A clue in an investigation
senses.definition: a piece of information that suggests where to look next
senses.definitionCN: 提示下一步该往哪里查的信息
senses.example: The police followed a new lead.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追查了一条新线索。
senses.why: A lead is something that leads you somewhere; in an investigation it is the information that pulls the search forward.
senses.whyCN: lead 是能把你带到某处的东西；在调查里，它就是推动搜查往前走的信息。

intro.en: Lead comes from an Old English verb meaning to cause to go, and it has kept the picture of someone walking in front.
intro.cn: lead 来自古英语中意为「使……走」的动词，一直保留着「有人走在前面」的画面。

items.en: Lædan meant to cause someone to go, to guide or to bring along a way.
items.cn: lædan 意为使某人走、引导或沿路带领。

items.en: The reconstructed verb *laidijan is related to the noun for a path or way.
items.cn: 重构动词 *laidijan 与表示「道路、路径」的名词有关。

items.en: Middle English leden keeps the sense of guiding and adds the idea of being first in a group.
items.cn: 中古英语 leden 保留引导义，并添上「在群体中最先」的意思。

items.en: The noun lead, meaning the first place, appears in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 表示第一名的名词 lead 在十五世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English adds lead to 'cause' and lead as a clue, while the metal lead is a different word with a different vowel.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 lead to（导致）与「线索」义；金属铅则是另一个词，元音也不同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections and relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for guiding and being first.
note.cn: 形近组收动词的变形与同族词；近义组收表示引导与领先的词。

entries.definition: Most important or in first place.

normalIntro.en: The past tense led drops the a of the present, and the family shows how guiding, leading and causing are one motion.

normal.en: The past tense is led, not leaded: lead, led, led.
normal.cn: 过去式是 led，不是 leaded：lead、led、led。

normal.en: Leader adds -er: the one who leads.
normal.cn: leader 加 -er，指带路的人。

normal.en: Lead to means to cause a result, as a road leads to a town.
normal.cn: lead to 意为导致结果，就像路通向城镇。

normal.en: Take the lead means to move into first place.
normal.cn: take the lead 意为取得领先。

normal.en: The metal lead is spelled the same but pronounced /led/ and has a different origin.
normal.cn: 金属铅拼写相同但读 /led/，词源也不同。

abstract.en: A word for walking in front turns into a word for authority because direction is a kind of decision.
abstract.cn: 一个「走在前面」的词变成「权力」的词，因为方向本身就是一种决定。

abstract.en: Lead to shows that causation is imagined as a path with a destination.
abstract.cn: lead to 说明因果关系被想象成一条有终点的路。

abstract.en: A clue is called a lead because information, too, can point a way.
abstract.cn: 线索被称为 lead，因为信息也能指出一条路。

examples.en: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「走在前面」；由带路扩展到掌权、导致结果、处于领先，以及为调查指路。

core_image: 两面墙相遇的那条线，扫帚总爱把灰尘扫到那里
scene: 放学后我在书店门口等人，书店就在十字路口附近。 I stood waiting at the corner of the street.
sceneCN: 这里 corner 是「街角」（第 2 个义项：两条街交汇处）；句意是我在街角等人。

senses.title: The place where two lines or surfaces meet
senses.definition: the point or area where two edges, walls or surfaces meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条边、两面墙相交的点或区域
senses.example: The cat likes to sleep in the corner of the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫喜欢睡在教室的角落里。
senses.why: Two walls closing in form a small hidden space, the picture of a corner.
senses.whyCN: 两面墙相夹形成隐蔽小空间，这正是角落的画面。

senses.title: The place where two streets meet

senses.exampleCN: 我们学校附近的街角有家小书店。

senses.title: To force someone into a difficult position

senses.example: The question cornered him, and he had to tell the truth.

senses.why: A person at the corner has walls on two sides and nowhere to run.
senses.whyCN: 被逼到角落的人两侧是墙，无处可逃。

senses.title: A difficult or remote position
senses.definition: a difficult situation or a distant small place

senses.example: The club helps students in far corners of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家社团帮助城市偏远角落的学生。
senses.why: Corners are far from the centre, so they stand for distant places or hard spots.

intro.en: Corner is not about corn at all, though it sounds like it.
intro.cn: corner 虽然听起来像 corn，却与谷物无关。

items.en: The Latin word cornu meant a horn, the hard point on an animal's head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cornu 意为角，即动物头上的坚硬尖角。

items.en: Old French turned cornu into corniere, the horn-shaped point.
items.cn: 古法语把 cornu 变成 corniere，指角状的尖点。

items.en: Norse hornna reinforced the horn idea in northern speech.
items.cn: 北欧语 hornna 在北方语言中强化了角的意象。

items.en: English blended these forms into corner in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语把多种形式融合成 corner。

items.en: Later corner spread from walls to streets, sports fields and even traps.
items.cn: 后来 corner 从墙角扩展到街角、球场，甚至引申为困境。

note.en: Some words share the horn root, others rhyme with corner.
note.cn: 有的词共享「角」词根，有的与 corner 押韵形似。

definition_en: giving attention to what you do so that you avoid mistakes, harm or danger
core_image: 端着一碗满出来的热汤，眼睛盯着脚下的每一步
scene: 科学课上，老师提醒大家做实验时要格外小心。 The teacher reminded us to be careful during the science experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 careful 是「小心的」（第 1 个义项：留神以免出错或受伤）；句意为老师提醒做实验要小心。

derivatives.zh: 由 careful 加 -ly 构成，义为「小心地；仔细地」
由 careful 加 -ness 构成，义为「小心；仔细」

senses.title: Paying attention to avoid harm
senses.definition: taking care so that you do not get hurt or cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 留神以免自己受伤或伤到别人
senses.example: Be careful when you cross the street.
senses.exampleCN: 过马路时要小心。
senses.why: Care began as a burdened mind, and a burdened mind watches every step.
senses.whyCN: care 本是挂心之事，挂心的心自会看清每一步。

senses.title: Doing things thoroughly and exactly
senses.definition: doing something with close attention so it is done well
senses.definitionCN: 用心细看细做，把事情做好
senses.example: She gave a careful answer to the question.
senses.exampleCN: 她对问题作了细致的回答。
senses.why: The same watchfulness, turned to work, becomes thoroughness.
senses.whyCN: 这份警觉用到做事上，便成了周密细致。

intro.en: Careful is simply care plus the suffix full, a mind full of care.
intro.cn: careful 就是 care 加上后缀 full——一颗装满挂念的心。

items.en: Old English caru laid the root of worry.
items.cn: 古英语 caru 奠定忧虑之根。

items.en: Middle English carful meant full of anxiety or sorrow.
items.cn: 中古英语 carful 指满心忧虑或悲伤。

items.en: The suffix -ful mirrors French -ful-like endings meaning full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 对应法语「充满」类后缀。

items.en: The worry sense softened into watchful attention.
items.cn: 忧虑义软化成留神注视。

items.en: Today careful means both safe handling and thorough work.
items.cn: 今天 careful 兼指安全操作与细致做事。

note.en: The first group collects word-family relatives; the second collects attention words.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词，第二组收集注类词。

entries.definition: Not taking care; making mistakes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗心的」，是 careful 的反义词。

entries.definition: Happy and smiling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高兴的」，后缀相同。

entries.definition: Good to use; helpful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有用的」，同用 -ful 后缀。

entries.definition: Careful to avoid danger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谨慎的」，侧重避险。

entries.definition: Watching and listening closely.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「专注的」，侧重留意。

entries.definition: Complete and careful in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「彻底周到的」，与细心义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember careful as care plus full.
normalIntro.cn: 把 careful 看成 care 加 full。

normal.en: careful = care + ful, a heart full of care.
normal.cn: careful 即「装满小心的心」。

normal.en: be careful of traffic near school.
normal.cn: 上学路上当心车流。

normal.en: carefully is the adverb form.
normal.cn: carefully 是其副词形式。

normal.en: careless is the opposite with -less.
normal.cn: careless 是带 -less 的反义词。

normal.en: a careful plan leaves nothing out.
normal.cn: 周密的计划滴水不漏。

abstract.en: Walk an icy path in your mind, one slow step at a time.
abstract.cn: 在心里走一段冰路，一步一缓。

abstract.en: Hold a full bowl level and watch the liquid.
abstract.cn: 端平满碗，眼盯汤面。

abstract.en: See a detective reading every line twice.
abstract.cn: 想象侦探把每行字读两遍。

examples.en: Please be careful with the knife.
examples.cn: 用刀请务必小心。

examples.en: She is careful about her homework.
examples.cn: 她做作业很细心。

examples.en: A careful check found the small mistake.
examples.cn: 细致的检查发现了那个小错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯尔福」——凯尔全福，因为他做事处处小心。

root: 古英语 caru（忧虑）+ 后缀 -ful（充满）→ 中古英语 carful → 现代英语 careful；同族 careless、carefully、carefulness。

sensesIntro.en: Careful turns a full heart into safe hands and thorough work.
sensesIntro.cn: careful 把装满挂念的心变成稳当的手与细致的活。

core.cn: 核心意象：装得太满、于是步步留神的心

definition_en: concerning all or most cases, not specific or detailed, or a top army officer
core_image: 鸟瞰整个战场的高地指挥台：既见全局，也见执旗的将军
scene: 战报室里地图铺满整面墙。 The general studied the front line before giving any order.
sceneCN: 这里 general 是「将军」（第 5 个义项：高级军官）；句意为将军在下达任何命令前先研究前线态势。

derivatives.zh: general 加 -ly 构成，义为「通常；大体上」
general 加 -ize 构成，义为「概括；推广到一般」
generalize 的名词形式，义为「概括；泛化结论」

senses.title: Covering all or most cases
senses.definition: including or affecting all or most people, things, or cases
senses.definitionCN: 包含或影响所有人、物或情形
senses.example: There is general agreement on the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对新规则已有普遍共识。
senses.why: The Latin root means of a kind or class, so the covering-everything sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「属于同一类」，因此「覆盖全体」是最古老的意义层。

senses.title: Not detailed or specific
senses.definition: giving the main points without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 只给要点、不展开细节
senses.example: She gave a general outline of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她给出了计划的大致轮廓。
senses.why: Looking at the whole rather than the parts yields the rough-sketch sense.
senses.whyCN: 看整体而非局部，便得到「粗线条」这一义项。

senses.title: Higher in rank, as general manager
senses.definition: having overall responsibility, as in general manager
senses.definitionCN: 负有全面职责，如总经理
senses.example: The general manager signs every contract.
senses.exampleCN: 每一份合同都由总经理签署。
senses.why: One who oversees the whole class of affairs is placed over it, extending the covering sense to rank.
senses.whyCN: 统管一类事务的人被置于其上，「覆盖」义由此延伸到职务层级。

senses.title: The ordinary public
senses.definition: ordinary people, as in the general public
senses.definitionCN: 普通人们，如 the general public
senses.example: The museum opens its doors to the general public on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆每逢周五向公众开放。
senses.why: The broad mass is contrasted with the specialist few, so the crowd receives the general label.
senses.whyCN: 广大人群与少数专家相对，于是大众获得了「一般」的标签。

senses.title: A top army officer
senses.definition: an officer of the highest army rank above colonel
senses.definitionCN: 陆军中高于上校的最高级军官
senses.example: The general reviewed the troops at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 将军在拂晓检阅部队。
senses.why: The officer in charge of the whole army took the name of the whole itself, general.
senses.whyCN: 统率全军者以「全体」之名为衔，即 general（将军）。

senses.title: Generalize to a rule
senses.definition: to form a wide rule from single cases, as a verb use
senses.definitionCN: 从个别情形形成普遍规则的动词用法
senses.example: Do not generalize from one bad experience.
senses.exampleCN: 不要凭一次糟糕经历就下一般性结论。
senses.why: Pulling particulars into one class is the Latin sense in motion, so the verb was formed.
senses.whyCN: 把个别收拢为一类正是拉丁词根义的运动形式，动词由此造出。

intro.en: General comes from Latin genus, the race or kind of a thing, later carried through French into English.
intro.cn: general 来自拉丁语 genus（种属），后经法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin genus meant birth, race, kind, and gave the stem gener-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 genus 意为出生、种族、种类，给出词干 gener-。

items.en: Latin generalis meant belonging to a whole class or kind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 generalis 意为「属于整个类别」。

items.en: Old French general passed the adjective into learned and everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 general 把这一形容词带入书面与日常使用。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it for general, overall, and widespread.
items.cn: 中古英语借入它表示总体的、全面的、普遍的。

items.en: The army rank arose because the officer commanded the whole body of troops.
items.cn: 军衔义源于该军官统率整支军队，故称 general。

items.en: Modern English added the adverb, the verb generalize, and the public sense.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了副词、动词 generalize 与大众义。

note.en: General splits into an adjective of breadth and a noun of rank, with generate family nearby.
note.cn: general 分为「广度」形容词与「军衔」名词，generate 词族就在近旁。

abstract.en: One flag among many flags: the general among officers.

scene: 村口的公告板前围了几个人，纸上写着一行字，边角被风吹得卷起。 She read the message twice before walking home.
