senses.title: Information sent to someone
senses.definition: a piece of information, news or a request that one person sends to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个人传给另一个人的一条信息、消息或请求
senses.example: She read the message twice before walking home.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。
senses.why: Latin mittere meant to send, so a message is literally the thing sent; the word names the content by the act of carrying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」，所以 message 字面上就是「被送出的东西」；这个词是用「传递」这一动作来给内容命名的。

senses.title: The central idea of a speech or work
senses.definition: the main point or lesson that a speech, book, film or advertisement wants its audience to take away
senses.definitionCN: 演讲、书籍、电影或广告希望受众记住的核心观点或教训
senses.example: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。
senses.why: If a message is what is sent, then a work of art also sends something, and the word shifts from the paper to the point the author wants delivered.
senses.whyCN: 既然 message 是被送出的东西，艺术作品也在送出东西，于是词义就从那张纸转到作者想送达的那层意思。

senses.title: A formal official communication
senses.definition: a formal written or spoken statement sent by a government, a leader or an organization to a body or the public
senses.definitionCN: 政府、领导人或组织向机构或公众发出的正式书面或口头说明
senses.example: The president sent a message to Congress on the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 总统就新预算向国会提交了一份咨文。
senses.why: Because sending is neutral, the same word can serve ceremony as well as chat, and officials borrowed it for statements that must be on record.
senses.whyCN: 因为「送」本身是中性的，同一个词既可服务闲谈也可服务仪式，官方便借它来指必须留档的说明。

senses.title: To send a message to someone
senses.definition: to send a written or electronic message to a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某个群体发送书面或电子信息
senses.example: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。
senses.why: Once the noun names the thing sent, it easily becomes a verb: people began to message each other as soon as a channel existed.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的是被送出的东西，它就很容易变成动词：一有了传递渠道，人们就开始互相 message。

intro.en: Message comes from the same Latin verb as mission and missile, and it reached English through French as the name for what is sent.
intro.cn: message 与 mission、missile 同出一个拉丁动词，经法语进入英语，本义就是「被送出的东西」。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, to dispatch or to let go, and it stands behind mission, missile and message alike.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、派遣、放出，mission、missile 与 message 都由它而来。

items.en: The participle missus meant sent, and the derived noun named a sending or something dispatched.
items.cn: 分词 missus 意为「送出的」，由它派生的名词指一次发送或被送出之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin missaticum named a message or an errand, literally the business of one who is sent.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum 指消息或差事，字面是被派出者所办的事。

items.en: Old French message meant news or a communication carried by word or letter, and it entered English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 message 指口头或书信传递的音信，诺曼时期之后进入英语。

items.en: Modern English widened message to the point of a film, then narrowed it again to texts and chats when new channels appeared.
items.cn: 现代英语把 message 扩展到作品的要旨，等到新渠道出现，又把它收回到短信与聊天上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin sending family; the near-meaning group collects short communications and written notices.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「送」的词族；近义组收简短的通信与书面通知。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message between two places.
entries.definitionCN: 在两地之间传递消息的人。

entries.definition: A formal or humorous word for a letter that is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 对「发出的信件」的正式或戏谑说法。

entries.definition: A portion of food sent to table, later disorder; the same sending verb lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 端上桌的一份食物，后来指混乱；背后的动词同样是「送」。

entries.definition: A task or journey given to someone who is sent to do it.
entries.definitionCN: 交给被派出者去完成的差事或行程。

entries.definition: A short written record or a few lines left for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，或留给某人的几行字。

entries.definition: A short internal notice sent between members of an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 组织成员之间传阅的简短内部通知。

entries.definition: A written or printed statement that tells people something.
entries.definitionCN: 告知人们某事的书面或印刷说明。

entries.definition: The broader act of passing information, by speech, writing or signal.
entries.definitionCN: 通过说话、书写或信号传递信息的更宽泛行为。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to what is dispatched, who carries it, and the point it is meant to deliver.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到被送出之物、送它的人，以及它想送达的那层意思。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, so a message is the thing that has been sent.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，所以 message 就是被送出去的那样东西。

normal.en: Missaticum in medieval Latin named an errand or a message, the business of a person who is sent.
normal.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的 missaticum 指差事或消息，即被派出者要办的事。

normal.en: Messenger adds -er to the same stem, naming the person who carries the message.
normal.cn: messenger 在同一词干后加 -er，指送消息的人。

normal.en: Message and mess share the verb mittere, one naming what is sent, the other the dish sent to a table.
normal.cn: message 与 mess 共用 mittere，一个指被送出的东西，一个指送到桌上的菜。

normal.en: Get the message is the idiom built on arrival: the information has reached you and you understand it.
normal.cn: get the message 这一成语建立在「送达」上：信息到了你这里，你也懂了。

abstract.en: A word for a thing sent shows that meaning always needs a carrier, a route and a receiver before it counts as communication.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「被送出之物」的词说明：意思必须先有载体、路线与接收者，才算完成了传递。

abstract.en: The same word covers a note, a film and a presidential address, because all three ask someone to receive something.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖便条、电影与总统咨文，因为三者都在请人接收某样东西。

abstract.en: When the phone lit up, the old noun quietly became a verb, proof that a word changes shape when a new channel appears.
abstract.cn: 手机亮起时，这个古老的名词悄悄变成了动词，证明新渠道出现时词也会改换形态。

examples.en: She read the message twice before walking home.
examples.cn: 她把那条留言读了两遍才走回家。

examples.en: The message of the film is that small kindnesses travel further than grand promises.
examples.cn: 这部电影的要旨是：细小的善意比宏大的承诺传得更远。

examples.en: He messaged the whole team as soon as the train stopped.
examples.cn: 火车一停，他就给全队发了消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹塞纸」——妹妹把写好的纸条塞进门缝，那就是一条留言；记住 message 是消息。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送）→ missus（送出的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 missaticum（差事、消息），经古法语 message 进入英语；同族词多与传送、派遣有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something sent from one person to another; the senses divide into a piece of news, the point a work delivers, an official statement and the act of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从一个人送到另一个人的东西；义项分为一条音信、作品要送达的意思、官方说明，以及发送这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board nailed up at the entrance of a village, a paper note flapping at the corner, a few people leaning in to read it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块钉在村口的公告板，纸条边角被风吹起，几个人凑近读上面的字。

branches.en: a note slipped under a door
branches.cn: 塞在门缝下的纸条

branches.en: a clerk handing a sealed letter across a desk
branches.cn: 职员隔着桌子递出封好的信

branches.en: an audience leaving a theatre still arguing
branches.cn: 看完戏仍在争论的观众

branches.en: a speech read aloud in a formal hall
branches.cn: 正式大厅里被朗读的文件

branches.en: a phone lighting up on a pillow
branches.cn: 枕边亮起的手机

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of sending, its participle, the medieval noun for an errand, the French form and two English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「送」的拉丁动词、它的分词、指差事的中世纪名词、法语形式，以及两个英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 明亮的；鲜艳的；聪明的；前景光明的
definition_en: full of light, strong in colour, quick to learn, or likely to succeed
core_image: 阳光直射进屋、整面窗户发亮
scene: 早晨的阳光照进教室，整面窗户亮得让人睁不开眼。 Morning sun filled the classroom and the bright window hurt his eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 bright 是「明亮的」（第 1 个义项：光线充足）；句意为晨光洒进教室，明亮的窗户晃得他睁不开眼。

pos.zh: 形容词：明亮的；鲜艳的；聪明的；有希望的

derivatives.zh: 由 bright 加 -ly 构成，义为「明亮地；鲜艳地」
由 bright 加 -ness 构成，义为「明亮；亮度」
由 bright 加 -en 构成，义为「使明亮；变得明朗」

senses.title: Full of light
senses.definition: giving out or reflecting a lot of light
senses.definitionCN: 发出或反射大量光线的
senses.example: The bright window hurt his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 明亮的窗户晃得他睁不开眼。
senses.why: Old English beorht meant shining, and light is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beorht 意为「发亮的」，光线是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Strong in colour
senses.definition: strong and easy to see, said of colours
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浓烈醒目、容易看见
senses.example: She wore a bright red coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件鲜红的外套。
senses.why: A strong colour reflects more light, so the sense of shining spread from light to colour.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色反射更多光线，于是「发亮」的意思从光扩展到了颜色。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: quick to learn and understand things
senses.definitionCN: 学得快、理解得快的
senses.example: He is a bright student who learns fast.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个学得很快的聪明学生。
senses.why: A bright mind was pictured as a lit room, where ideas can be seen clearly.
senses.whyCN: 聪明的头脑被想象成一间点亮的屋子，里面的想法清晰可见。

senses.title: Likely to succeed
senses.definition: full of promise, likely to be good
senses.definitionCN: 充满希望、很可能变好的
senses.example: The team has a bright future.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队前途光明。
senses.why: A good future is pictured as a lit road ahead, in contrast with a dark one.
senses.whyCN: 美好的未来被想象成前方一条明亮的道路，与昏暗的路形成对照。

intro.en: Bright began as a word for shining light, and from light it spread to colour, mind and future.
intro.cn: bright 最初指发亮的光，随后从光扩展到颜色、头脑与未来。

items.en: Beorht meant shining, full of light.
items.cn: beorht 意为发亮的、充满光的。

items.en: German brecht and Dutch bricht carry a nearby sense of shining.
items.cn: 德语 brecht 与荷兰语 bricht 都带有发亮的意思。

items.en: The form became bright, and the word kept light as its centre.
items.cn: 词形变为 bright，词义仍以光为中心。

items.en: A lit room made a good picture for a quick mind, so bright gained a sense of clever.
items.cn: 点亮的屋子很适合比喻机敏的头脑，于是 bright 获得了「聪明」的意思。

items.en: Today bright covers light, colour, intelligence and a promising future.
items.cn: 今天 bright 覆盖光线、颜色、智力与充满希望的未来。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about light and intelligence.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与光、智力有关的词。

entries.definition: The act of flying through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞行」，读音与 bright 接近。

entries.definition: A disease that damages plants.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「枯萎病」，拼写与 bright 相近。

entries.definition: Correct, or the opposite of left.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的；右边的」，读音与 bright 接近。

entries.definition: Giving out a clear, steady light.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「发光的；闪亮的」。

entries.definition: Quick to learn and good at solving problems.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聪明的；机灵的」。

entries.definition: Very strong and clear, said of colours or pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「鲜艳的；生动的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English beorht meant shining, and light is still the first sense.
normal.cn: 古英语 beorht 意为发亮，光至今仍是第一个义项。

normal.en: A strong colour reflects more light, so bright also means vivid.
normal.cn: 浓烈的颜色反射更多光，所以 bright 也指鲜艳。

normal.en: A lit room made a good picture for a quick mind, so bright also means clever.
normal.cn: 点亮的屋子很适合比喻机敏的头脑，所以 bright 也指聪明。

normal.en: It often pairs with light, colours, idea and future.
normal.cn: 它常与 light、colours、idea、future 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-i-g-h-t; the gh is silent.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-i-g-h-t，其中 gh 不发音。

abstract.en: See sunlight pouring through a window and filling a whole room: that room is bright.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光穿过窗户，照亮整间屋子：那间屋子就是 bright。

abstract.en: Move the same light behind a person's eyes and the word turns into cleverness.
abstract.cn: 把同一束光移到一个人的眼睛后面，这个词就变成了「聪明」。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the lit room bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那间明亮的屋子把意思带回来。

examples.en: The bright window hurt his eyes.
examples.cn: 明亮的窗户晃得他睁不开眼。

examples.en: She wore a bright red coat.
examples.cn: 她穿了一件鲜红的外套。

examples.en: The team has a bright future.
examples.cn: 这支球队前途光明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不来特」——阳光照进屋子，满屋发亮：明亮的

root: bright 来自古英语 beorht，意为发亮的、充满光的，与德语 brecht、荷兰语 bricht 有相近含义。词义以光为中心，随后扩展到浓烈的颜色；点亮的屋子又被用来比喻机敏的头脑，于是它获得「聪明」的意思；前方明亮的道路则引申出「有希望的」。今天 bright 覆盖光、颜色、智力与前途。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bright grow from one picture: a strong light that makes things easy to see.
sensesIntro.cn: bright 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：一束让万物清晰可见的强光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight filling a room through a window
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光穿过窗户照亮整间屋子

branches.en: THE LIGHT: giving out light is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 光线线：发出光线是最字面的第一个义项。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: strong colour reflects the same light.
branches.cn: 颜色线：浓烈的颜色反射同样的光。

branches.en: THE MIND: a lit room stands for a quick mind.
branches.cn: 头脑线：点亮的屋子比喻机敏的头脑。

branches.en: THE FUTURE: a lit road ahead stands for a good prospect.
branches.cn: 前途线：前方明亮的路比喻美好的前景。

branches.en: THE GLOW: light and colour both make a thing easy to see.
branches.cn: 亮光线：光与颜色都让事物清楚可见。

intro.en: Bright is a base adjective, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: bright 是基础形容词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin clarus means bright and clear; it is a parallel word, not the source of bright.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clarus 意为「明亮、清楚」，它是平行词，不是 bright 的来源。

items.example: Beorht is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: beorht 是有记录的古英语形式。

items.meaning: the energy that lets us see

definition_en: the state of being known or talked about by many people, especially for achievement
core_image: 一座聚光灯下的讲台，台上人的一句话被成千上万张嘴传开
scene: 颁奖礼上主持人宣布得主，全场起立鼓掌，闪光灯连成一片。 Winning the prize brought her fame overnight.
sceneCN: 这里指「名声」，对应第 1 个义项：被许多人谈论的状态；句意为获奖让她一夜成名。画面要点：奖杯、闪光灯、起立鼓掌的人群。

collocations.zh: 成名之事；值得一提之处

derivatives.zh: 著名的（同根形容词：被许多人谈论的）
声名狼藉的（否定前缀 in- 加同根词，坏的那半名声）
恶名（同根名词，指坏名声）
诽谤（前缀 de- 加词根 fam-，把名声说坏）
有名的（过去分词作形容词）

senses.title: The state of being widely known
senses.definition: the condition of being known or talked about by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人知晓或谈论的状态
senses.example: She achieved fame at twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十岁就成名了。
senses.why: To be spoken of by many is to exist in many mouths; the root meant exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 被众人谈论即活在众人之口；词根本义正是如此。

senses.title: A good public reputation
senses.definition: a positive reputation for achievement or quality
senses.definitionCN: 因成就或品质而得的正面名声
senses.example: The town won fame for its pottery.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇以陶器闻名。
senses.why: Rumor splits: what is said can be praise; the good half is fame.
senses.whyCN: 传闻会分裂：所言可为赞美；好的那一半即声望。

senses.title: Renown in a field or era
senses.titleCN: 某一领域或时代的盛名
senses.definition: lasting recognition within a profession or period
senses.definitionCN: 在某一行业或时期获得的持久认可
senses.example: His fame rests on three novels.
senses.exampleCN: 他的盛名建立在三部小说之上。
senses.why: Recognition that outlives the moment is fame with a long tail.
senses.whyCN: 超越一时的认可即带着长尾的 fame。

intro.en: Fame comes from Latin fama, 'what people say', the same root that gives famous and infamy.
intro.cn: fame 来自拉丁语 fama「人们所说的」，与 famous、infamy 同根。

items.en: Latin fama meant report, rumor, and public opinion; fari meant to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fama 意为传闻、舆论；动词 fari 意为说。

items.en: Old French fame and the learned form renommee carried the sense of public repute.
items.cn: 古法语 fame 及其雅化形式传递「公众声誉」之义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed fame in the thirteenth century, both as rumor and as renown.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 fame，兼指传闻与声望。

items.en: Modern English narrowed fame to positive renown, leaving rumor to another word.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fame 收窄为正面声望，传闻之义让给了别的词。

items.en: Mass media made fame a currency: celebrities are famous for being famous.
items.cn: 大众传媒使 fame 成为一种通货：名人因有名而有名。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fam- (speak of); near-meaning words name degrees of being known.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fam-（被谈论）；近义组命名「知名」的不同程度。

entries.definition: the adjective built on fame
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词：fame 的形容词形式

entries.definition: evil reputation
entries.definitionCN: 恶名；同根反义

entries.definition: gas or smoke; an angry mood
entries.definitionCN: 气体；怒气；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: widespread and admired fame
entries.definitionCN: 盛名；声望（更书面）

entries.definition: the general opinion of a person
entries.definitionCN: 名誉；可好可坏

entries.definition: a famous person; modern fame
entries.definitionCN: 名人；现代式名气

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for being talked about.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「被谈论」之词的五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fama meant what people say: fame lives in other people's mouths.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fama＝人们所说的：fame 活在他人的口中。

normal.en: famous, infamy, and defame all carry the same speaking root.
normal.cn: famous、infamy、defame 都含「说」这一词根。

normal.en: a hall of fame is a room full of people everyone talks about.
normal.cn: hall of fame（名人堂）就是满是众口相传之人的一间屋。

normal.en: fame was once rumor too; English gave the rumor job to another word.
normal.cn: fame 一度也指传闻；英语把传闻的活儿交给了别的词。

normal.en: claim to fame means the thing that makes you known.
normal.cn: claim to fame 指让你成名的那件事。

abstract.en: Fame is a crowd's echo of one person's name.
abstract.cn: 名声是人群对一个人名字的回声。

abstract.en: A reputation is a shadow: it follows you and outgrows you.
abstract.cn: 名誉是影子：跟着你，还长得比你大。

abstract.en: Spoken words build ladders; enough of them and the ladder holds a name above the crowd.
abstract.cn: 话语垒成梯子，垒得够多，名字就被举到人群之上。

examples.en: The scientist sought truth rather than fame.
examples.cn: 这位科学家追求真理而非名声。

examples.en: The dish brought the little restaurant local fame.
examples.cn: 这道菜让小餐馆在本地出了名。

examples.en: His fame spread far beyond his own country.
examples.cn: 他的名声远播本国之外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费姆」——费用名目多，人人谈论你，就是 fame（名声）。

root: 拉丁语 fama（传闻、舆论），来自动词 fari（说）。经古法语 fame 进入中古英语，兼指传闻与声望；现代英语收窄为正面名声。同根词 famous、infamy、defame。

sensesIntro.en: From being spoken of outward to good repute and lasting renown.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被谈论」扩展到良好声誉与持久盛名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name traveling from mouth to mouth across a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字在人群中口口相传。

branches.en: THE KNOWING: the state of many mouths.
branches.cn: 知名：众口相传的状态。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: the good half of what is said.
branches.cn: 赞誉：所言之中好的那一半。

branches.en: THE LASTING: renown that survives its season.
branches.cn: 持久：超越一时的盛名。

branches.en: THE CURRENCY: fame as media capital.
branches.cn: 通货：名声作为媒体资本。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: reputation that follows and outgrows its owner.
branches.cn: 影子：跟随主人并比主人更长久的名誉。

intro.en: Fame carries the Latin speaking root fam- through a family of names and reputations.
intro.cn: fame 携拉丁「说」之词根 fam- 构成一族名字与声誉之词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fama and fari seed the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fama 与 fari 孕育整个词族。

items.example: the article led to a defamation suit
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章招致诽谤诉讼

definition_en: the reflexive pronoun for the speaker, used when the speaker is the object, for emphasis, or in the phrase by myself meaning alone
core_image: 镜子里的人抬手，镜外的手也同时抬起，两边是同一个人
scene: 厨房里，砧板和菜刀摆在水池边，洋葱刚切到一半。 I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里是「我自己」（第 1 个义项：反身用法，动作回到主语本身）；句意为切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。图中可辨识物件：砧板、菜刀、洋葱。

derivatives.zh: myself 中的 self 部分，义为「自身、自我」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」
由 self 加 -less 构成，义为「无私的」

senses.title: The speaker as the object of his own action
senses.definition: used as the object when the subject and the object are the same speaker
senses.definitionCN: 主语和宾语是同一个人（说话人）时用作宾语
senses.example: I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。
senses.why: English marks a returning action with a compound of the owner word and self, so the doer appears a second time inside the sentence as the one acted on.
senses.whyCN: 英语用「所有者词加 self」的复合形式标记回到自身的动作，于是动作发出者在句中第二次出现，成了被作用的人。

senses.title: The speaker, emphasized
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was the speaker and no one else
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词后或句末，强调是说话人本人而不是别人
senses.example: I built these shelves myself.
senses.exampleCN: 这些架子是我自己搭的。
senses.why: The same compound can stand outside the verb's arguments and simply point at the speaker, which turns a reflexive into a spotlight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合形式可以站在动词论元之外，单纯指向说话人，于是反身代词变成了一束追光。

senses.title: Alone, without company
senses.definition: used with by to say that the speaker is without other people
senses.definitionCN: 与 by 连用，表示身边没有别人
senses.example: I went to the cinema by myself.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人去看了电影。
senses.why: If the speaker is the only one present, the returning self has no one else to lean on, so the reflexive phrase comes to mean solitude.
senses.whyCN: 如果只有说话人在场，那个回到自身的「我」没有别人可以依靠，反身短语于是引申出「独处」的意思。

intro.en: Myself joins the English possessive my to self, a Germanic word for one's own person that Old English already used in reflexive compounds.
intro.cn: myself 把英语所有格 my 与 self 结合；self 是日耳曼语中表示「自身」的词，古英语已用它构成反身复合形式。

items.en: A stem reconstructed as selbho- is often proposed for the reflexive family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 常有人为这一族反身词提出重构形式 selbho-，但该重构并不确定。

items.en: The adjective selbaz meant the same person or the very one, and it supplied the base for self.
items.cn: 形容词 selbaz 意为「同一个人、正是那个人」，为 self 提供了基础。

items.en: Old English seolf or self could stand alone as a pronoun and appear in compounds with possessive forms.
items.cn: 古英语 seolf 或 self 可单独作代词，也能与所有格形式组合。

items.en: Middle English wrote combinations such as mi self as two words, and the pattern spread to every person of the pronoun.
items.cn: 中古英语把 mi self 这类组合写成两个词，这一模式扩展到人称代词的每一人称。

items.en: Modern English fused the parts into myself, added the emphatic and the by-phrase uses, and kept the plural pattern ourselves.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合并为 myself，发展出强调用法和 by 短语用法，并保留了复数形式 ourselves。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the parallel reflexives for other persons; the near-meaning group holds the bare pronouns and the idea of being alone.
note.cn: 形近组收其他人称的平行反身代词；近义组收不带 self 的代词以及「独自一人」这层意思。

entries.definition: The reflexive for the person spoken to, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 听话人的反身代词，构造方式相同。

entries.definition: The reflexive for a male third person.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称男性的反身代词。

entries.definition: The reflexive for we, with the plural selves.
entries.definitionCN: we 的反身代词，用复数形式 selves。

entries.definition: The reflexive for it, used for things and animals.
entries.definitionCN: it 的反身代词，用于事物和动物。

entries.definition: The plain object pronoun, used where the action does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的宾格代词，动作不回到自身时使用。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun that myself points back to.
entries.definitionCN: 主格代词，myself 所指回的对象。

entries.definition: The general reflexive for an unspecified person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某人的反身代词。

entries.definition: Without other people present, the sense carried by by myself.
entries.definitionCN: 身边没有别人，即 by myself 所表达的意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is my plus self, and the same recipe is repeated across the whole pronoun system.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 my 加 self，同一配方在人称代词的整套系统里反复使用。

normal.en: My plus self gives myself; the plural keeps the same recipe and changes my to our: ourselves.
normal.cn: my 加 self 得到 myself；复数沿用同一配方，把 my 换成 our，得到 ourselves。

normal.en: When the subject and the object are the same person, English uses the self form: I hurt myself, not I hurt me.
normal.cn: 主语和宾语是同一个人时，英语用带 self 的形式：说 I hurt myself，不说 I hurt me。

normal.en: Myself cannot be the subject of a finite verb; emphasis uses I myself or a final myself instead.
normal.cn: myself 不能充当限定动词的主语；要强调可以用 I myself，或把 myself 放在句末。

normal.en: By myself means alone; beside myself means out of control, not standing next to the body.
normal.cn: by myself 意为独自；beside myself 意为情绪失控，而不是站在身体旁边。

normal.en: In including myself, the self form works after a preposition or at the end of a list.
normal.cn: 在 including myself 里，这个反身形式用在介词后或列表末尾。

abstract.en: A mirror is the plainest picture of a sentence that turns back on its speaker.
abstract.cn: 镜子是一个句子折回说话人时最直白的画面。

abstract.en: A spotlight aimed at one person explains the emphatic use better than any rule.
abstract.cn: 一束只照一个人的追光，比任何规则都更能解释强调用法。

abstract.en: An empty cinema seat makes the meaning of by myself visible at once.
abstract.cn: 一个空着的电影院座位，一眼就能让人看见 by myself 的含义。

examples.en: I taught myself to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我自学弹吉他。

examples.en: I painted the whole fence myself.
examples.cn: 整道栅栏都是我自己刷的。

examples.en: I waited by myself for over an hour.
examples.cn: 我独自等了一个多小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买赛尔夫」——自己给自己买东西，就叫 myself，我自己。

root: my 与古英语 self（自身）复合而成；self 一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 selbaz，拉丁语 ipse 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the speaker turning back on the speaker; emphasis and solitude are two ways that turn becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是说话人把动作折回自己；强调用法与独处义，是这一折返的两种显形方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before a mirror, with the reflected hand rising at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前抬起一只手，镜中的手在同一刻也抬起。

branches.en: a cut finger held under the tap
branches.cn: 在水龙头下按住割伤的手指

branches.en: a sentence whose object is its subject
branches.cn: 宾语与主语是同一个人的句子

branches.en: a shelf built without help
branches.cn: 没有帮手也照样搭好的架子

branches.en: a ticket bought for one seat only
branches.cn: 只买了一个座位的票

branches.en: an empty row in a dark cinema
branches.cn: 黑暗影院里空着的一排座位

intro.en: The word is a compound of the possessive my and the Germanic self, and the same pieces recur in every reflexive pronoun.
intro.cn: 这个词由所有格 my 与日耳曼语的 self 复合而成，同样的部件在每个人称的反身代词中都会重现。

latinIntro.en: Latin has a reflexive pronoun of its own, but no form of it is a reliable source for self, so the cognate list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有自己的反身代词，但其中没有任何形式可以可靠地作为 self 的来源，因此同源词列表留空。

items.meaning: the speaker as object or emphasis

definition_en: the planet we live on, the ground, or the soil in which plants grow
core_image: 俯瞰脚下的大地：泥土、田野与整个星球
scene: 春耕的田埂上，翻起的泥土散发着湿润的气息。 Farmers turned the earth before planting the seeds.
sceneCN: 这里 earth 是「泥土、土壤」（第 3 个义项：植物生长所依赖的土）；句意：农民在播种前翻整了泥土。

forms.label: 复数（指土壤时常用单数）

derivatives.zh: earth 加 en 构成，义为「陶制的；土制的」
earth 加 quake 构成，义为「地震」
earthen 加 ware 构成，义为「陶器」

senses.title: The planet
senses.definition: the world, the planet on which people and animals live
senses.definitionCN: 人类与动物居住的星球，即世界
senses.example: The moon goes around the Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 月球绕着地球转。
senses.why: The ground under every foot, seen whole, is the planet itself.
senses.whyCN: 每只脚下的大地被整体看待，便是这颗行星。

senses.title: The ground surface
senses.definition: the surface of the ground, especially as opposed to the sky or sea
senses.definitionCN: 地面，尤指与天空或海洋相对的大地
senses.example: The plane fell back to earth.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机坠回地面。
senses.why: Whatever flies must finally meet the ground.
senses.whyCN: 凡飞行之物终将落回大地。

senses.title: Soil for plants
senses.definition: the substance in which plants grow; soil
senses.definitionCN: 植物赖以生长的物质；土壤
senses.example: She filled the pot with fresh earth.
senses.exampleCN: 她往花盆里填了新土。
senses.why: The whole ground narrowed to a handful of soil.
senses.whyCN: 整个大地缩小成一小把泥土。

senses.title: A burrow of a fox
senses.definition: a hole or tunnel where a wild animal such as a fox lives
senses.definitionCN: 狐狸等野生动物居住的洞穴
senses.example: The hounds followed the fox to its earth.
senses.exampleCN: 猎犬把狐狸追到了它的洞里。
senses.why: The ground opens to shelter what lives beneath.
senses.whyCN: 大地张开，庇护栖于其下的生灵。

intro.en: Earth is one of the oldest words in the language, naming the ground before anyone imagined planets.
intro.cn: earth 是语言中最古老的词之一，先命名脚下的大地，远在人们想象行星之前。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *ertho meant ground and soil.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *ertho 意为大地、土壤。

items.en: Old English eorthe covered ground, soil and the world.
items.cn: 古英语 eorthe 涵盖地面、土壤与世界。

items.en: Old Norse jǫrð, a sister form, kept the same meaning in the north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 jǫrð 是其姐妹形式，在北方保留相同词义。

items.en: In Middle English earth named the world itself, then the planet.
items.cn: 中古英语中 earth 先指世界本身，后指这颗行星。

items.en: Modern English added compounds like earthquake and earthworm.
items.cn: 现代英语又派生出 earthquake、earthworm 等复合词。

note.en: These words stand near earth in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 earth 相邻。

entries.definition: made of earth or baked clay
entries.definitionCN: 土制的；陶制的

entries.definition: the floor of a fireplace, different root
entries.definitionCN: 壁炉地面（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a worm that lives in soil
entries.definitionCN: 蚯蚓

entries.definition: the top layer of ground where plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 土壤

entries.definition: the solid surface of the earth
entries.definitionCN: 地面

entries.definition: dry ground as opposed to sea
entries.definitionCN: 陆地

normalIntro.en: Use the handful-of-soil picture and the earth family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「一把泥土」的画面和 earth 词族来记。

normal.en: the Earth with a big E is the planet.
normal.cn: 大写的 the Earth 指行星地球。

normal.en: turn the earth is what farmers do before sowing.
normal.cn: turn the earth 是农民播种前的翻土。

normal.en: down to earth means practical, like feet on soil.
normal.cn: down to earth 表示务实，像双脚踩在土上。

normal.en: earthquake is the earth that quakes.
normal.cn: earthquake 就是「会晃动的大地」。

normal.en: on earth in questions means in the world, ever.
normal.cn: 疑问句里的 on earth 相当于「究竟」。

abstract.en: Crumble a handful of dark soil between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 在指间捻碎一把深色的泥土。

abstract.en: Look down from the sky and see one whole round ground.
abstract.cn: 从天空俯瞰，看见一整块圆形的大地。

abstract.en: Feel the plane sinking until the ground receives it.
abstract.cn: 感受飞机下沉，直到大地把它接住。

examples.en: Rain soaked the earth around the young trees.
examples.cn: 雨水浸透了幼树四周的泥土。

examples.en: The Earth takes one year to go around the sun.
examples.cn: 地球绕太阳一周需要一年。

examples.en: He is honest and down to earth.
examples.cn: 他为人诚实而务实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄思」——挖土挖出「厄思」，满脑子都是大地

root: 来自原始日耳曼语 *ertho（大地、土壤），古英语 eorthe；本义为脚下之地，后升格为「世界」「地球」，又缩小为「泥土」。

sensesIntro.en: Earth rises from the soil in your hand to the ground, to the world, and to the whole planet.
sensesIntro.cn: earth 从手中的泥土升到地面，再到世界，最后到整颗行星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark soil held in an open hand
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手掌捧着深色泥土

branches.en: The round world seen whole
branches.cn: 被整体看待的圆形世界

branches.en: The solid surface under the sky
branches.cn: 天空之下的坚实表面

branches.en: The soft soil where roots grow
branches.cn: 根系生长的松软土壤

branches.en: The opening in the ground that shelters
branches.cn: 庇护生灵的地洞

branches.en: Whatever is dug from the ground
branches.cn: 一切从地里掘出之物

intro.en: Earth forms many compounds about ground things.
intro.cn: earth 派生大量与大地相关的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relative is terra, seen in terrestrial and territory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词是 terra，见于 terrestrial 与 territory。

latinEntries.meaning: earth, land; source of terrestrial, territory
